Sacrococcygeal Teratoma

MONDO:0042727 Pathograph 34 Show in embeddings browser extragonadal germ cell tumor

The commonest tumour of the newborn, and a germ cell tumour in a place with no gonad. It is thought to arise when a primordial germ cell migrating from the yolk sac to the gonadal ridge is left behind in the caudal midline and is reprogrammed to a pluripotent state, after which it differentiates into all three germ layers at once. Most are mature, and complete resection with clear margins is the treatment; about one child in ten recurs. Three things make it dangerous. Before birth, a large solid tumour steals so much cardiac output that the fetus goes into high-output failure and hydrops, which is what the prenatal predictors are for. In the first weeks after birth, bleeding, into the tumour or at its removal, was the commonest cause of death in a Dutch series. And a mature-looking tumour can recur as a yolk sac tumour years later, which is what the alpha-fetoprotein surveillance is for.

Discussions and Knowledge Gaps

4
Does fetal hydrops predict survival in sacrococcygeal teratoma?
CONTROVERSY OPEN sct_hydrops_predicts_or_not
Attached to
phenotypes#Hydrops fetalis pathophysiology#High-Output Cardiac State from Tumour Vascular Steal
Two cited sources answer this in opposite directions and neither is obviously wrong. One reports hydrops as a potential risk factor for poor outcome at an odds ratio of 21, from 68 analysed fetuses of an 84-fetus cohort with eleven poor outcomes, and a meta-analysis lists it among the factors predictive of poor outcome. The other, a review of 157 fetuses split across open surgery, percutaneous intervention and no intervention, reports that hydrops and cardiac failure had no significant impact on survival. The disagreement may be about what is being predicted - outcome in the first, survival in the second - or about selection: the fetuses who develop hydrops are the ones offered intervention. No cited source reconciles them, and the entry carries both rather than choosing.
Show evidence (3 references)
PMID:37964422 SUPPORT DIRECT PRIMARY RESULT Human clinical
"Factors associated with poor outcome in fetuses with prenatally diagnosed SCT were cardiomegaly, hypervascular tumor, solid tumor morphology, fetal hydrops, and placentomegaly."
One side, from a meta-analysis of eleven studies and 447 patients.
PMID:38731178 REFUTE DIRECT PRIMARY RESULT Human clinical
"In our evaluation, we determined that the presence of fetal hydrops and cardiac failure had no significant impact on survival in SCT cases."
The other side. REFUTE against the claim above, and recorded here rather than averaged into it.
PMID:23845611 SUPPORT DIRECT BACKGROUND Human clinical
"Some fetuses with sacrococcygeal teratoma (SCT) develop hydrops, but there is no consensus on an appropriate prognostic marker for poor prognosis."
The absence of consensus, stated in those terms by a third study. It predates both sources above and the disagreement outlived it.
Every cited animal model of teratoma is gonadal. Does the mouse germ cell teratoma mechanism apply to a tumour whose defining feature is that the germ cell never reached a gonad?
HUMAN MODEL MISMATCH OPEN sct_no_disease_model
Attached to
pathophysiology#Epigenetic Reprogramming to a Pluripotent State animal_models#Mouse
The reprogramming step in this entry's chain is supported entirely by mouse work, and every mouse in the cited literature has a testicular or ovarian teratoma. No sacrococcygeal model exists in any species in this corpus; the only non-rodent animal report is an oropharyngeal teratoma in a goat. That matters more here than in most entries, because the thing being modelled is a cell that failed to reach the gonad, and the model contains one. The mouse work also fails in a way that is informative: mutating Dnd1 alone gives germ cell loss rather than teratoma, and the strains built to make testicular teratomas made ovarian ones instead.
Show evidence (2 references)
PMID:33568756 NO_EVIDENCE DIRECT BACKGROUND Model organism
"This suggests that other genes are involved in teratoma formation."
The authors' own reading of the first failure. NO_EVIDENCE: it records that the mechanism is incomplete rather than bearing on whether it transfers to this disease.
PMID:29378702 SUPPORT INDIRECT BACKGROUND Model organism
"Spontaneous testicular teratoma develops from primordial germ cells (PGCs) in embryos; however, the molecular mechanisms underlying teratoma formation are not fully understood."
The state of the mechanism, and the organ it was worked out in. BACKGROUND: it is the paper's framing of the problem.
Which prenatal measurement, at which threshold, should decide whether a fetus with sacrococcygeal teratoma is offered intervention?
KNOWLEDGE GAP OPEN sct_prenatal_threshold_unsettled
Attached to
diagnosis#Prenatal ultrasound with tumour volume to fetal weight ratio
At least ten thresholds compete in the cited literature and none has displaced the others: tumour volume to fetal weight ratio at 0.12 before 24 weeks and 0.11 before 32 weeks; the same ratio at 0.095 for fetal outcome against 0.12 for maternal operative risk; total tumour volume over estimated fetal weight at 0.16; a solid tumour volume index at 0.09; a morphology score of 3; tumour volume over head circumference plus polyhydramnios at 3.0; growth velocity at 7 mm per week; a solid tumour to head volume ratio of 1; tumour volume over biparietal diameter at 60 cm3 per cm; and a volume growth rate above 18.01 cm3 per week and a volume above 245 cm3. The ratio's validation study reports that none of the factors associated with poor prognosis was an independent predictor on multivariate analysis; the growth velocity study reports that its measure was the only one that survived stepwise regression, and a second growth series that only the volume growth rate survived adjustment. One series finds the solid tumour volume index a better predictor than total volume over fetal weight, and another finds no significant difference between the ratio and the head-circumference composite. Each comes from 10 to 79 fetuses. The entry records all of them, with their denominators, because a reader choosing between them needs to see that the choice has not been made.
Show evidence (2 references)
PMID:23845611 NO_EVIDENCE DIRECT BACKGROUND Human clinical
"Some fetuses with sacrococcygeal teratoma (SCT) develop hydrops, but there is no consensus on an appropriate prognostic marker for poor prognosis."
The gap stated as a gap. NO_EVIDENCE: it records the absence rather than bearing on which marker is right.
PMID:25783370 SUPPORT DIRECT BACKGROUND Human clinical
"Attempts at defining predictors of poor outcome in fetal sacrococcygeal teratoma (SCT) have been hampered by small patient numbers."
Why the gap persists, from a three-centre series that evaluated 79 fetuses and excluded eleven terminations.
The Altman types are the postnatal classification most frequently referenced for this tumour. Two cited series restate their definitions, quoted below, but the entry does not curate the types. Should they be curated from those restatements, or from the primary source once it can be read?
KNOWLEDGE GAP OPEN sct_altman_unsourceable
Attached to
pathophysiology#Tridermal Teratomatous Mass at the Sacrococcyx
Types II and III carry an odds ratio of 1.6 for recurrence in the largest cohort, and the classification predicts no long-term sequela in the Dutch national questionnaire study, although a 2023 systematic review found that abnormal bladder function differed by Altman type, lowest in type I (18%) and highest in type IV (60%). The entry records those results and does not curate the types. The primary source, the 1974 American Academy of Pediatrics Surgical Section survey, caches with an empty body under both its PMID and its DOI - both files are committed with this entry so the gap is checkable from the repository - and a classification cannot be transcribed from a covariate column. Two imaging sources cited here for other findings restate all four types, citing earlier work, and one gives the usual share of each; they are quoted below and would let the types be curated with evidence behind them. The two restatements differ in detail: one calls type I the majority of cases, the other gives the four shares as 45, 35, 10 and 10%, and they word type IV differently. HPO's own text definition of HP:0030736, the term this entry binds for the mass, also states all four types, and HPO carries separate terms for types I, II and III with their own definitions and one for the presacral type IV, but an ontology definition is not a literature source and cannot be an evidence snippet.
Show evidence (5 references)
PMID:39248311 NO_EVIDENCE INDIRECT PRIMARY RESULT Human clinical
"Altman type II or type III, and immature or malignant histology were associated with recurrence."
What the entry can say about the classification: its association with recurrence, from 3407 children. NO_EVIDENCE for the question above, which is about the definitions.
PMID:17560233 SUPPORT DIRECT PRIMARY RESULT Human clinical
"Age at completion of the questionnaire, Altman classification, sex, and histopathology were not risk factors for any long-term sequelae."
A negative result for the same classification on a different outcome, which is the other thing the entry can say about it without defining it.
PMID:36326365 SUPPORT DIRECT BACKGROUND Human clinical
"Type I: developing only outside the fetus (can have a small presacral component); the majority of cases, Type II: extra-fetal with intra-pelvic presacral extension, Type III: extra-fetal with abdominopelvic extension, Type IV: tumor developing entirely in the fetal pelvis."
The four types, restated in a fetal MRI series' methods with a citation to the classification.

Pathophysiology

8
Primordial Germ Cell Left in the Caudal Midline
A germ cell that does not complete the migration from the yolk sac to the gonadal ridge. The midline distribution of extragonadal germ cell tumours is the main evidence for this: the tumours appear where the migration route runs.
primordial germ cell CL:0000670 Cell Ontology (CL) Relation: this pathophysiological event involves this cell type This pathophysiological event involves primordial germ cell (CL:0000670). CL:0000670 is a cell type from the Cell Ontology.
germ cell migration GO:0008354 Gene Ontology (GO) Relation: this pathophysiological event involves this biological process This pathophysiological event involves germ cell migration (GO:0008354). GO:0008354 is a biological process from the Gene Ontology.
Downstream
Epigenetic Reprogramming to a Pluripotent State A germ cell in the wrong place does not become a tumour by being there. What converts it is a return to pluripotency; no cited source shows the conversion happening in a human sacrococcygeal tumour, and the mouse work that does show it is testicular.
Show evidence (2 references)
DOI:10.1111/j.1365-2605.2007.00793.x SUPPORT INDIRECT REVIEW SYNTHESIS Human clinical
"Their distribution along the midline of the body is still best explained by the migration of primitive germ cells during development."
The argument for this node, and the authors' own measure of how settled it is: still best explained, which is a statement about competing hypotheses rather than a demonstration. INDIRECT because an anatomical distribution is an inference step from a cell's history.
PMID:33906346 SUPPORT DIRECT REVIEW SYNTHESIS Human clinical
"SCT is the most common type I GCT and is believed to originate through epigenetic reprogramming of early primordial germ cells migrating from the yolk sac to the gonadal ridges."
Names the cell and the route this node binds, and keeps the hedge: believed to originate. The second half of the sentence is the next node.
Epigenetic Reprogramming to a Pluripotent State
The misplaced germ cell reacquires the capacity to make all three germ layers. The bound process is stem cell population maintenance, which is the nearest GO has: searching GO for reprogramming and for pluripotency returns nothing, and this term's own definition ends by allowing that stem cells may arise de novo from other cell types. In mouse testicular teratoma this step has a named mechanism - loss of DND1 lowers EZH2 and H3K27me3 at a cell-cycle gene, and the germ cells reprogramme to pluripotent stem cells - and that is a different organ and a different strain background from this disease.
pluripotent stem cell CL:0002248 Cell Ontology (CL) Relation: this pathophysiological event involves this cell type This pathophysiological event involves pluripotent stem cell (CL:0002248). CL:0002248 is a cell type from the Cell Ontology.
stem cell population maintenance GO:0019827 ↑ INCREASED Gene Ontology (GO) Relation: this pathophysiological event involves this biological process This pathophysiological event involves increased stem cell population maintenance (GO:0019827). GO:0019827 is a biological process from the Gene Ontology.
Animal models
Dnd1 mutant 129/Sv mouse (Ter) Mouse recapitulates The only cited source that shows the reprogramming step happening, with a named chromatin mechanism and both a loss-of-function and a rescue arm.
MC4R G25S congenital mouse strains Mouse partially recapitulates These strains do form germ cell teratomas, so they reach the node; they reach it in the wrong organ. Four of them gave ovarian teratomas where testicular ones were expected, and the authors call that result surprising. The paper also states, as background, that Dnd1-mutant mice show germ cell loss rather than teratoma, which reads against the other cited mouse paper reporting that Dnd1 mutation enhances teratoma formation in 129/Sv. The strain behind the germ cell loss sentence is not given in the cached abstract, so this entry cannot say whether the two results are a genuine disagreement or two strains behaving differently.
Downstream
Tridermal Teratomatous Mass at the Sacrococcyx A pluripotent cell differentiating in all three directions is what the mass is made of.
Show evidence (2 references)
PMID:29378702 SUPPORT INDIRECT PRIMARY RESULT Model organism
"In addition, Ezh2 expression or Ccnd1 deficiency repressed the reprogramming of PGCs into pluripotent stem cells, which mimicked the conversion of embryonic germ cells into teratoma-forming cells."
The reprogramming step and a necessity test for it, in mouse embryos: restoring EZH2 or removing cyclin D1 represses the conversion. The authors' own word for what it models is mimicked.
PMID:32999426 SUPPORT INDIRECT PRIMARY RESULT Human clinical
"Teratomas had higher expression of ectodermal genes, suggesting a tridermal nature."
The human end of this node, from a 51-sample paediatric germ cell tumour cohort: the expression profile of teratomas is consistent with three germ layers. The cohort includes extragonadal samples but never names the sacrococcygeal site, so this is a property of teratoma as a class.
Tridermal Teratomatous Mass at the Sacrococcyx
The tumour. Mature in most neonates, with immature or frankly malignant components in a minority, and arising attached to the coccyx. Its size, its solidity and how fast it grows are what decide the fetal course; its histology and the completeness of its removal are what decide the rest.
Downstream
Sacrococcygeal mass The mass as the finding: detected before birth in just over half of affected pregnancies in a national register; the study's abstract names no method of detection and does not say when the rest were found.
High-Output Cardiac State from Tumour Vascular Steal A large, solid, highly vascular tumour is a low-resistance circuit in parallel with the fetus. The fetal heart compensates by raising output, and past a point it fails. This is the arm every prenatal predictor in this entry is trying to anticipate.
Haemorrhage into the Tumour In a Dutch series, internal tumour haemorrhage was among the commonest causes of early death and, like the other common causes, strongly associated with larger tumour size. The series reports the association with size, not how the tumour comes to bleed.
Malignant Yolk Sac Component Yolk sac tumour either present from the start and missed, or arising later within a mature teratoma. No cited source settles which, and the meta-analysis that raises the question names both possibilities without choosing.
Pelvic and Perineal Mass Effect The tumour and its removal both act on the same small anatomical space, which carries the nerves and sphincters of bowel and bladder. No cited source separates the damage the tumour does from the damage the operation does, and of the variables the Dutch national study examined, its abstract reports only one as a risk factor: tumour size, for an unacceptable scar.
Show evidence (2 references)
PMID:33142194 SUPPORT DIRECT BACKGROUND Human clinical
"Neonatal SCTs are mostly mature, but can also contain immature and/or malignant components."
The histological composition of the mass, from a meta-analysis of 22 articles and 1516 patients.
PMID:23773720 SUPPORT DIRECT BACKGROUND Human clinical
"Sacrococcygeal teratoma is the most common neonatal tumor."
Where this tumour sits among neonatal neoplasms, stated by one of the prenatal-imaging series. BACKGROUND: it is the paper's opening sentence rather than its result.
High-Output Cardiac State from Tumour Vascular Steal
Combined ventricular output above 625 mL/min/kg with abnormal Doppler or echocardiographic findings is the definition one series used. Cardiomegaly, abnormal venous preload indices and umbilical venous pulsation are the signs; hydrops is the end of it.
Downstream
Placentomegaly An enlarged placenta accompanies the high-output state, alongside hydrops and cardiomegaly. The review groups all three as factors associated with cardiac failure, which is the relation this edge draws; it does not say which of them produces which, so the edge runs through unknown intermediates rather than recording a measured sequence.
Stillbirth The fatal end of this arm. The register reports the outcome without attributing each death to a mechanism, so the edge is drawn through unknown intermediates: high-output failure and hydrops are the route the other cited sources describe, not one this register measures.
Hydrops fetalis The decompensated end of the high-output state, and the point at which fetal intervention is considered.
Cardiomegaly The heart's response to the sustained output demand, and a predictor of poor outcome in its own right.
Polyhydramnios Excess amniotic fluid accompanies the severe form. One cited series states, in its review of the literature, that the raised cardiac output contributes to it, without saying how; a systematic review found it much commoner among non-survivors managed without intervention.
Premature birth Delivery is earlier when the fetus is compromised, and earlier delivery is itself what several series find associated with death. One cited series names a route in its review of the literature: the raised output contributes to polyhydramnios, which can lead to preterm birth by distending the uterus. Whether early delivery causes the deaths or marks the fetuses already failing, the cohort data quoted here cannot say.
Maternal mirror syndrome In one case the mother's illness began shortly after the fetus showed early signs of right heart failure, before overt hydrops, and resolved after delivery; the same report says the syndrome is usually associated with severe fetal hydrops. A second case report's discussion cites earlier work linking the arteriovenous shunts of a large tumour to cardiac failure, placentomegaly, hydrops and the syndrome, and says the placenta has been suggested as its source, because ending the pregnancy resolves the maternal oedema. No cited source demonstrates the mechanism, so the edge runs through unknown intermediates.
Neonatal death High-output cardiac failure is one of the commonest causes of early death, with internal tumour haemorrhage and bleeding at operation.
Show evidence (2 references)
PMID:23773720 SUPPORT DIRECT PRIMARY RESULT Human clinical
"Outcomes measured were survival, hydrops or high cardiac output state, defined as a combined ventricular output of >625 mL/min/kg with abnormal Doppler or echocardiogram findings."
One of two numerical cut-offs for ventricular output in the cited sources, and one series' operating definition rather than a validated threshold. The other, a combined ventricular output above 550 ml/min/kg, is one of four echocardiographic signs in a cohort that mixes this tumour with twin reversed arterial perfusion.
PMID:15192290 SUPPORT DIRECT PRIMARY RESULT Human clinical
"The most important prognostic criteria were cardiomegaly, fetal hydrops, and increased preload indexes of the fetal venous system as sign of fetal heart failure."
The signs of this node, from a sonographic series.
Haemorrhage into the Tumour
Bleeding into the tumour. With high-output failure and bleeding at operation it is one of the commonest causes of early death, and all three are strongly associated with larger tumours. The Dutch series that reports this gives risk factors for haemorrhagic death - prematurity, a tumour volume above 1000 cm3 and emergency operation - and its abstract does not split haemorrhagic deaths by source, so those risk factors are not shown to be specific to bleeding into the tumour.
Downstream
Neonatal death Death after birth from bleeding. In the Dutch series internal tumour haemorrhage was among the commonest causes of early death; nine children died within 27 days of birth, seven of the deaths related to tumour haemorrhage, circulatory failure or both, and haemorrhagic deaths, which the abstract does not split by source, were almost 70% of the neonatal mortality. Neither of the last two figures is specific to bleeding into the tumour.
Show evidence (3 references)
PMID:27502009 SUPPORT DIRECT PRIMARY RESULT Human clinical
"High-output cardiac failure, internal tumor hemorrhage and perioperative bleeding were the most common causes of early death and were all strongly associated with larger tumor sizes."
Internal tumour haemorrhage among the commonest causes of early death in a Dutch series of 235 children.
PMID:30949371 SUPPORT DIRECT PRIMARY RESULT Human clinical
"In our case the histologic examination of the tumor demonstrated signs of bleeding; nevertheless the presence of an arteriovenous shunt was not examined."
Histological signs of bleeding in the resected tumour, in a case that ended in fetal death; whether the tumour carried an arteriovenous shunt was not examined.
PMID:27502009 SUPPORT INDIRECT PRIMARY RESULT Human clinical
"Risk factors for hemorrhagic mortality were prematurity, tumor volume>1000cm3 and performance of an emergency operation."
The risk factors for haemorrhagic death in the Dutch series. Indirect for this node: the abstract does not split haemorrhagic deaths by source, and bleeding at operation is among its causes of early death.
Malignant Yolk Sac Component
Yolk sac tumour, the malignant histology this tumour recurs as. Microscopic foci of it inside an otherwise mature teratoma raise the recurrence rate sharply, which is the practical reason the whole specimen is examined rather than sampled.
Downstream
Elevated serum alpha-fetoprotein The marker the malignant component secretes, and the thing surveillance measures.
Malignant recurrence Recurrence with malignant histology, which is what makes recurrence matter. It can be very late: many occur within one to six years and some as long as twenty years after diagnosis; no cited source gives the fraction in that window.
Show evidence (2 references)
PMID:39016163 SUPPORT DIRECT PRIMARY RESULT Human clinical
"We identified 56 patients with mature SCT, of which 9 (16%) demonstrated microscopic YST."
How often the microscopic component is present in tumours called mature, in a single-institution series.
PMID:39016163 SUPPORT DIRECT PRIMARY RESULT Human clinical
"Recurrence was more likely in patients with microscopic YST [5/9 (56%) vs. 2/47 (4%), p = 0.021] and positive margins [6/24 (35%) vs. 1/32 (3.1%), p = 0.030]."
What it does to the recurrence rate, with the margin status beside it. Nine patients in the exposed arm, so read it as a signal rather than a rate.
Pelvic and Perineal Mass Effect
The consequences that outlast the tumour. In the Dutch national questionnaire study of long-term survivors, nearly half reported impaired bowel function or urinary incontinence and 40% an unacceptable scar. Its authors conclude that clinical variables cannot clearly identify the patients at higher risk; on univariate analysis the one variable its abstract reports as a risk factor for any of them is tumour size above 500 cm3, for the scar. A single-centre series' review of the literature reports that the complications listed in one passage, early and late and mostly obstructive and bowel problems, are commoner in tumours with a larger intrapelvic component; that passage does not list incontinence or the scar; the series' introduction names incontinence and aesthetic concerns among long-term complications without tying them to the intrapelvic part.
Downstream
Cosmetically unacceptable surgical scar The scar is left by the resection this node's consequences follow from, not by the mass itself. It sits here because the Dutch national study counts it alongside the bowel and bladder sequelae as one of the three long-term problems that affect quality of life.
Bowel incontinence Soiling or involuntary bowel movements after resection, in about a fifth of long-term survivors.
Urinary incontinence Reported by just under a third of long-term survivors.
Constipation The commonest single bowel complaint in the Dutch national questionnaire study, at 17%.
Pelvic and Sacral Nerve Injury Functional sequelae are reported more often after resection of a tumour with a large intrapelvic extension, and abnormal bladder function differs by Altman type; the entry places injury to the pelvic and sacral nerves between the tumour's extent and that dysfunction, a step these abstracts do not measure. A 2022 MRI series restates tumour compression or infiltration of the sacral nerves among the tumour's complications, without measuring it. The Dutch national questionnaire study found no long-term sequela associated with Altman type. The mass effect's own edges to the two incontinence phenotypes carry that study's figures; this route carries that restatement and the factors that go with dysfunction.

"There were 46% who reported impaired bowel function and/or urinary incontinence (9% involuntary bowel movements, 13% soiling, 17% constipation), and 31% urinary incontinence."
The breakdown, from 79 of 99 posted questionnaires at a median age of 9.7 years. A questionnaire study with an 80% response, so read it as the experience of those who answered.
PMID:17560233 SUPPORT DIRECT PRIMARY RESULT Human clinical
"Patients who are at higher risk for the development of long-term sequelae cannot be clearly assessed using clinical variables."
The authors' conclusion on prediction; the one positive result its abstract reports, tumour size for the scar, is the next item.
PMID:17560233 SUPPORT DIRECT PRIMARY RESULT Human clinical
"Size of the tumor (>500 cm3) was a significant risk factor for cosmetically unacceptable scar"
The one clinical variable the abstract reports as a risk factor for a sequela, on univariate analysis.

Pelvic and Sacral Nerve Injury
Injury to the pelvic and sacral nerves. A 2022 MRI series restates tumour compression or infiltration of the sacral nerves among the tumour's complications, and a 1990 series attributes leg weakness to sciatic nerve palsy without saying what caused the palsy. The operation as a second cause is the entry's inference: none of the sources cited on this node names a surgical nerve injury, and the 2020 series' surgical injury is to the pelvic organs. The other cited sources give associations rather than a measured mechanism: functional sequelae were commoner after resecting large intrapelvic tumours by an abdominoperineal approach (67% in the 1990 series); in a 2020 single-centre series the patients with functional disorders had a low 1-minute Apgar score, larger tumours needing abdominosacral resection, surgical injury to the pelvic organs and immature or malignant histology; and a 2023 systematic review associates higher Altman type, unfavourable tumour biology and reoperation with poor function. The Dutch national questionnaire study found neither Altman type nor histopathology to be a risk factor for any long-term sequela.
Downstream
Urinary incontinence Abnormal bladder function differed by Altman type in a 2023 systematic review, lowest in type I (18%) and highest in type IV (60%), with types II and III at 37.7% and 32.4% (p = 0.007), and adverse urological outcomes were commoner in patients who needed reoperation and with immature or malignant tumours; in a Swedish series univariate analysis found urinary tract dysfunction correlated with immature histology, and the abstract reports only low gestational age as an independent predictor. A 2022 MRI series restates nerve compression leading to incontinence. The Dutch national questionnaire study found neither Altman type nor histopathology to be a risk factor for any long-term sequela, urinary incontinence included. These are factors that go with dysfunction; no cited source measures the nerve injury itself.
Bowel incontinence Anorectal dysfunction after resection; in the 2020 series the patients with functional disorders, who by the abstract's counts all had anorectal dysfunction, had larger tumours, surgical injury to the pelvic organs and immature or malignant histology, and in a Swedish series bowel dysfunction correlated with tumour size on univariate analysis. A 2022 MRI series restates nerve compression leading to incontinence. The 2023 systematic review found that bowel dysfunction had no significant association with tumour characteristics. These are factors that go with dysfunction; no cited source measures the nerve injury itself.
Lower limb weakness Leg weakness from sciatic nerve palsy, in 2 of 27 children in a 1990 series.

Medical Actions

Complete resection with the coccyx
Action: tumour resectionNCI Thesaurus (NCIT) Relation: this treatment is this clinical intervention This treatment is tumour resection, annotated with Tumor Resection (NCIT:C164212). NCIT:C164212 is a clinical intervention from the NCI Thesaurus. Ontology label: Tumor Resection NCIT:C164212
Platform: Surgery
The definitive treatment, done after birth in most patients. Completeness is what matters: positive margins raise the recurrence rate about tenfold in one series, and incomplete resection is named as a risk factor for recurrence by a review. The coccyx is removed with the tumour: two series report doing so in their own patients, and a review names failure to remove it among the primary drivers of recurrence.
Mechanism Target:
BYPASSES Tridermal Teratomatous Mass at the Sacrococcyx — Resection removes the mass. It acts on nothing above it - the misplaced germ cell and whatever reprogrammed it are not addressed - which is the reason a complete resection is followed for years rather than discharged.

Fetal radiofrequency ablation of the feeding vessels
Action: radiofrequency ablationNCI Thesaurus (NCIT) Relation: this treatment is this clinical intervention This treatment is radiofrequency ablation (NCIT:C15666). NCIT:C15666 is a clinical intervention from the NCI Thesaurus. Ontology label: Radiofrequency Ablation NCIT:C15666
Platform: Surgery
Interrupting the tumour's blood supply before birth, to reverse the high-output state rather than to remove the tumour. The first report of it is also the clearest statement of its limit: ablating most of the tumour mass was unnecessary and killed two of four fetuses. In a 2024 systematic review survival was 45.8% (22 of 48) after percutaneous procedures as a group and 12 of 18 (67%) after radiofrequency ablation itself, against 71.0% (66 of 93) without intervention; in a 2011 cohort it was 6 of 8 after fetal intervention (radiofrequency ablation in six, shunting alone in two) against 14 of 14 without, an outcome the authors call similar despite the treated fetuses' worse prognostic features. The groups are not alike: in the review fetal intervention is indicated for fetuses with hydrops or cardiac dysfunction, and hydrops and cardiac failure were rarer without it; in the 2011 cohort the treated fetuses' tumours were larger, rapidly growing and more often vascular, with associated polyhydramnios or cardiomegaly. The review says it could not evaluate the effectiveness of fetal surgery of any type against no fetal intervention.
Mechanism Target:
INHIBITS High-Output Cardiac State from Tumour Vascular Steal — The target is the shunt, not the tumour. Reducing flow through the feeding vessels is enough to reverse the failure; the tumour is resected after birth.

Open fetal resection
Action: open fetal resection of the tumourNCI Thesaurus (NCIT) Relation: this treatment is this clinical intervention This treatment is open fetal resection of the tumour, annotated with Tumor Resection (NCIT:C164212). NCIT:C164212 is a clinical intervention from the NCI Thesaurus. Ontology label: Tumor Resection NCIT:C164212
Platform: Surgery
Resection of the tumour in utero for a fetus in progressive high-output failure. The field has moved away from it towards the minimally invasive techniques above, and the cited survival figures do not separate the two by much. Survival after open surgery was 56.2% (9 of 16) in a 2024 systematic review, against 71.0% (66 of 93) without intervention. The review reports survival as significantly higher without intervention than in the cohorts treated by fetal surgery, without a p-value for that comparison and without saying whether it holds for open surgery alone, but says it did not aim to compare the two, because fetal intervention is indicated for the severe forms with hydrops or cardiac dysfunction, and that it could not evaluate the effectiveness of fetal surgery of any type against no fetal intervention.
Mechanism Target:
INHIBITS High-Output Cardiac State from Tumour Vascular Steal — Removing the tumour before birth removes the shunt. The cost is maternal morbidity and preterm delivery, which is why the alternative above exists.

Delivering early, between 27 and 32 weeks, in response to impending fetal or maternal decompensation, and resecting the tumour straight after birth, instead of fetal surgery or waiting. In one centre's series 9 of 11 fetuses delivered this way survived and none died of prematurity; the authors, reporting favourable outcomes in the absence of hydrops before 27 weeks or tumour rupture in utero, say their single-centre experience supports pre-emptive delivery for selected cases.
Mechanism Target:
INHIBITS High-Output Cardiac State from Tumour Vascular Steal — Ends the shunt by removing the tumour after birth, without operating on the fetus. The case report that restates the series names the absence of high-output cardiovascular failure, of tumour bleeding and of fetal anaemia among the conditions for its success.

Caesarean section for a large or vascular tumour
Action: caesarean sectionNCI Thesaurus (NCIT) Relation: this treatment is this clinical intervention This treatment is caesarean section, annotated with Cesarean Section (NCIT:C46088). NCIT:C46088 is a clinical intervention from the NCI Thesaurus. Ontology label: Cesarean Section NCIT:C46088
Platform: Surgery
When the tumour is large (more than 5 to 10 cm across) or highly vascular, vaginal birth is not recommended because of a higher risk of rupture and bleeding. The mode of delivery is chosen case by case; in a 2025 single-centre series 8 of the 9 delivered fetuses, two of them not detected before birth, were born by caesarean section, and the ninth by a spontaneous precipitous vaginal delivery. A tumour that is large for the fetus's weight also predicts a higher-risk maternal operation: a 2019 single-centre study counted open fetal surgery, classical caesarean delivery and EXIT as such operations, and a tumour volume to fetal weight ratio above 0.12 at or before 24 weeks predicted one.
Mechanism Target:
INHIBITS Haemorrhage into the Tumour — Avoids the rupture and bleeding that a vaginal birth risks with a large or highly vascular tumour; haemorrhage into the tumour is the nearest node the entry has for bleeding at birth.

Biochemical Markers

3
Serum alpha-fetoprotein (Physiologically high at birth and falling over the first months of life; raised for the child's age, or rising, with a malignant yolk sac component)
Pathograph Readouts
Readout of Malignant Yolk Sac Component Positive Monitoring
In follow-up for recurrence, a readout of the malignant yolk sac component. In a systematic review its sensitivity for malignant recurrence was 96%; the review cautions that its sensitivity to detect recurrence could be overestimated, because levels are mainly reported in patients with raised levels or at recurrence. In the Dutch cohort the level rose in malignant recurrences but did not predict mature or immature recurrence, and a normal value did not rule recurrence out.

Diagnosis

4
Prenatal ultrasound with tumour volume to fetal weight ratio
The test that finds the tumour and the one the risk stratification is built on. Tumour volume divided by estimated fetal weight above 0.12 before 24 weeks is the threshold the field uses; it was derived in ten fetuses and validated in a three-centre series that evaluated 79 and excluded eleven terminations.
obstetric ultrasonography NCIT:C217447 NCI Thesaurus (NCIT)
The threshold is not settled. The validation study reports 0.12 before 24 weeks with an area under the curve of 0.913. A second study reports both 0.12 before 24 weeks and 0.11 before 32 weeks, so those two are one measure at two gestational windows rather than rival values. A third finds that 0.095 predicts poor fetal outcome while 0.12 predicts increased maternal operative risk - the same number used for two different questions. Beside them sit a total tumour volume over estimated fetal weight of 0.16, a solid tumour volume index of 0.09, a morphology score of 3, a composite of tumour volume over head circumference plus polyhydramnios at 3.0, growth velocity at 7 mm per week, a solid tumour to head volume ratio of 1, a tumour volume over biparietal diameter of 60 cm3 per cm, and a volume growth rate above 18.01 cm3 per week and a volume above 245 cm3. One cited series finds the solid tumour volume index a better predictor than total tumour volume over fetal weight, and another finds no significant difference between the ratio and the head-circumference composite; two growth series each report that one growth measure alone stayed independent in their own data; no cited source compares all of them. The entry records all of them, and the validation study states that none of the factors associated with poor prognosis was an independent predictor on multivariate analysis.

Sacral mass on prenatal ultrasound
A heterogeneous mass arising from the sacral region, solid, cystic or mixed, with a variable blood supply. Signs of a high-output heart on fetal echocardiography
Abnormal size and systolic function of the fetal heart, including a raised combined ventricular output. In a series of 19 fetuses with this tumour or a twin reversed arterial perfusion sequence, every fetus that later died or developed hydrops had at least one of a cardiothoracic ratio above 0.5, a combined ventricular output above 550 ml/min/kg, tricuspid or mitral regurgitation, or a mitral valve Z-score above 2, and none of those who did well had any; diastolic function did not separate them. The 550 is that mixed cohort's cut-off for an abnormal output, and the entry's high-output node uses another series' definition of 625.

Progression

4
Prenatal
Detected before birth in 55% of pregnancies in a Finnish national register, and in 74% and 50% of cases in two other population-based series (only the Finnish abstract says what its share is counted over; see the prenatal detection row). In three hospital series of fetuses diagnosed before birth, the median week of diagnosis differs widely: 22 weeks in 55 fetuses, 23 in seven, and 30.9 in eleven. The high-output state is the route to a poor outcome that the prenatal predictors track, though a single-centre series of early delivery also reports a death from tumour rupture in the womb and one from pulmonary hypoplasia; fetuses that do well are delivered and operated on. Mortality including terminations is about a third in referral series and is driven by the terminations.

Recurrence
Duration: many recurrences within 1 to 6 years, some at 20 years
About one in ten children recur and about a third of those recurrences are malignant. The interval is the part that sets the follow-up: many recurrences fall within one to six years, in the pooled review's own word, and some are twenty years out. The risk of malignancy at initial resection rises with age and plateaus at six years, which is why delay matters.

The recommendation that follows, and the one the alpha-fetoprotein surveillance row implements.
Long-term survivorship
Survival is high. What survivors carry is functional: in the Dutch national questionnaire study, at a median age of about ten, nearly half reported impaired bowel function or urinary incontinence and 40% an unacceptable scar, and these sequelae were correlated with reduced quality of life. The study's authors conclude that clinical variables cannot clearly identify the patients at higher risk; the one risk factor its abstract reports is tumour size above 500 cm3, for the scar. Survival is also where this disease and the presacral teratoma of Currarino syndrome converge, at 94.9% against 96.9% in one global cohort, and malignancy is where they do not: malignant transformation at initial resection and malignant histology at recurrence are both several times higher here. Equal survival with unequal malignant risk is the reason the two are curated as separate entries rather than one. Later studies report predictors the Dutch national questionnaire study did not find, two of which, Altman type and histopathology, it tested and found not to be risk factors: in a 2023 systematic review abnormal bladder function differed by Altman type, and adverse urological outcomes were commoner with immature or malignant tumours and in patients who needed reoperation; low gestational age independently predicted both urinary tract and bowel dysfunction in a Swedish series. Two later results agree with the Dutch null: the review found no significant association of bowel dysfunction with tumour characteristics, and a Scottish national cohort, in which constipation was the commonest bowel complaint, found no obvious predictive features at presentation for its bowel findings. A UK nationwide study found documented adverse bladder or bowel dysfunction in 36% of 165 patients. Most respondents in the Swedish series still reported good or very good quality of life.

Epidemiology

4
Sex distribution
In a population-based birth defects registry in Hawaii, females accounted for 58.3% of the sacrococcygeal cases and 57.1% of the infant teratomas of all sites. The registry's teratoma rates, for all sites, differed by sex as by maternal race/ethnicity and geography, but apart from gestational age none of the differences was statistically significant, and its authors warn that the numbers are small. Two series give their own counts: among 55 neonates operated on between 1997 and 2016 who did not have a recurrence, excluding those who died and those with malignant germ cell tumours, 37 were female and 18 male; and an older series of 36 patients with benign neonatal tumours, treated from 1972 to 1990, reports 29 female patients as 89%, a share that does not fit 36 (29 of 36 is 81%). Three other sources restate a female excess of about 3:1, one of them 3:1 to 4:1, citing earlier work.

Differential Diagnoses

6

Conditions with similar clinical presentations that must be differentiated from Sacrococcygeal Teratoma:

Myelomeningocele Not Yet Curated MONDO:0019773
Overlapping Features A myelomeningocele and a sacrococcygeal teratoma can be taken for each other before birth. A case report describes a cystic tumour that mimicked a meningomyelocele; one centre, re-assessing two fetuses referred with a diagnosis of this tumour, found one to be healthy and the other to have a myelomeningocele; and a report of two presacral neuroblastomas names both conditions as the main clinical differentials in its two cases.
Distinguishing Features
  • In one case report, three-dimensional power Doppler imaging helped make the correct prenatal diagnosis of a cystic tumour that mimicked a meningomyelocele.
  • At one centre, assessment with both fetal MRI and ultrasound gave the right diagnosis in every fetus with this tumour assessed there, and re-assessment there re-classified one referral as a myelomeningocele.

Anterior sacral meningocele Not Yet Curated MONDO:0001147
Overlapping Features A meningocele in the presacral space, the space a sacrococcygeal teratoma with a presacral part occupies. A report of two siblings calls it and presacral teratoma related malformations that can both run in families, and both siblings had a presacral mass on imaging. Their family history of sacral bony abnormalities and anterior meningoceles resembles Currarino syndrome, although the abstract neither names the syndrome nor reports an anorectal malformation, and the siblings' presacral teratoma may be that syndrome's lesion rather than a sacrococcygeal teratoma; MONDO lists presacral teratoma as a synonym of sacrococcygeal teratoma, so the term alone does not settle it. No cited source reports an anterior sacral meningocele itself taken for a sacrococcygeal teratoma.

Fetus in fetu
Overlapping Features A malformed fetus-like mass within its host. A systematic review of 241 single and 33 multiple cases weighs a teratoma theory against an identical twin theory, finds evidence for both, and calls a monozygotic twin of the host the most likely explanation. It can be misdiagnosed as a teratoma because the two look alike on ultrasound, and it is rare at the sacrococcygeal site, where teratoma is common. In the review, the mass was found before birth in 43 of the single cases, and in three quarters of those it was not suspected on imaging; sacrococcygeal teratoma is among the presumptive diagnoses the review lists for a mass in the abdominal cavity. In its discussion the review calls telling fetus in fetu apart from highly differentiated teratomas crucial: it calls a teratoma a neoplasm originating from embryonic pluripotent cells, with the potential to behave in a malignant fashion, and fetus in fetu a parasitic twin within its host.
Distinguishing Features
  • A vertebral column or limb bones in the mass, with no immature elements: the systematic review calls a visible vertebral column or limb bones diagnostic and requires both conditions in its case definition, while noting that the defining criteria remain unclear. One or more long bones were detected in 131 of its 241 single cases, which the review says facilitated the diagnosis before surgery. A review of fetiform teratoma names cytogenetic studies as the gold standard for telling fetiform teratoma and fetus in fetu apart.
  • The site: 10 of the review's 241 single cases (4.1%) were sacrococcygeal, gluteal or perineal, against 174 (72.2%) retroperitoneal.
  • Fetiform teratoma, a germ cell tumour that can mimic a malformed fetus and also occurs at the sacrococcygeal site, lies on the teratoma side of the boundary; a review of it proposes the absence of a vertebral column and long bones as its criterion.
  • Organogenesis and a heartbeat: a case report's discussion calls well-differentiated organogenesis the key feature for telling fetus in fetu from teratoma, together with detection of a fetal heartbeat, citing earlier work. The systematic review, by contrast, documented heart or cardiac tissue in only 9 of its 241 single cases (3.7%) and calls heart tissue exceptionally rare in fetus in fetu.

Chordoma MONDO:0002894
Overlapping Features In children, sacrococcygeal chordoma is rare and may be confused with the teratoma, which the report calls more common and indolent. The report describes one adolescent. Distinguishing Features
  • Neither the case report's abstract nor the fetal MRI series gives an imaging, histological or marker feature that separates the two: the abstract contrasts chordoma's rarity in children with the teratoma, which it calls the more common and the indolent one, and the series only lists sacral chordoma among the differentials.

Animal Models

2
Dnd1 mutant 129/Sv mouse (Ter)
The classical teratoma mouse. Loss of DND1 drastically raises teratoma incidence, and the mechanism is worked out: DND1 suppresses a microRNA that inhibits EZH2, so its loss lowers H3K27me3 at a cell-cycle gene and the germ cells reprogramme.
Species
Mouse
Genotype
Dnd1 Ter (R178*) premature stop codon on the 129 background
Publication
PMID:29378702
Pathograph links
Epigenetic Reprogramming to a Pluripotent State recapitulates fidelity: moderate observes: molecular The only cited source that shows the reprogramming step happening, with a named chromatin mechanism and both a loss-of-function and a rescue arm.
Limitations: The tumours are testicular, not sacrococcygeal, and they arise in one inbred strain. No cited source reports a sacrococcygeal teratoma model in any species, so the step this link supplies is transferred across both organ and genetic background.
Divergences from the human mechanism
boundary omission qualifying
The model contains the gonad; this disease's defining feature is a germ cell that never reached one. Nothing in the model represents the caudal midline.
species mismatch qualifying
No DND1 variant is reported in human sacrococcygeal teratoma by any cited source, and the Ter allele's effect is confined to the 129 strain background.
Show evidence (2 references)
PMID:29378702 SUPPORT DIRECT PRIMARY RESULT Model organism
"Mutation of the dead-end 1 (Dnd1) gene, which encodes an RNA-binding protein, drastically enhances teratoma formation in the 129/Sv mouse strain."
What the model does, and the strain dependence that is one of its two recorded divergences.
+ 1 more reference
Notes
The targeted gene is named in the genotype and not bound. A model organism's own gene takes its model-organism database identifier, not the human HGNC one, and no MGI identifier for mouse Dnd1 could be resolved from any source available here: there is no local MGI build and the Alliance search endpoint returned nothing. Binding the human gene instead would put a mouse knockout on the human gene's page, which is the thing that rule exists to prevent.
MC4R G25S congenital mouse strains
A second teratoma locus, mapped and then edited. It is recorded here mainly for what it got wrong: the strains make teratomas, but in the wrong organ.
Species
Mouse
Genotype
LT-MC4R G25S point mutation, alone and with the Dnd1 Ter allele
Publication
PMID:33568756
Pathograph links
Epigenetic Reprogramming to a Pluripotent State partially recapitulates fidelity: low observes: organism These strains do form germ cell teratomas, so they reach the node; they reach it in the wrong organ. Four of them gave ovarian teratomas where testicular ones were expected, and the authors call that result surprising. The paper also states, as background, that Dnd1-mutant mice show germ cell loss rather than teratoma, which reads against the other cited mouse paper reporting that Dnd1 mutation enhances teratoma formation in 129/Sv. The strain behind the germ cell loss sentence is not given in the cached abstract, so this entry cannot say whether the two results are a genuine disagreement or two strains behaving differently.
Limitations: Neither result is in the caudal midline and neither is in a human, so the site this disease is defined by is outside the model. The organ the strain was built for is not the organ it produced.
Divergences from the human mechanism
boundary omission qualifying
The caudal midline is not in the model. Every teratoma these strains produce is gonadal, where this disease is extragonadal and sacrococcygeal, so the anatomical site and the tissues around it are outside the model's boundary.
species mismatch qualifying
Mouse germ cell teratoma is strain-restricted in a way human sacrococcygeal teratoma is not, and the strain backgrounds carrying these alleles have no human counterpart.
Show evidence (2 references)
PMID:33568756 SUPPORT DIRECT BACKGROUND Model organism
"However, the phenotype of mice with a mutated Dnd1 gene was germ cell loss."
The germ cell loss result, stated by the authors as background. Quoted here because it is what the apparent disagreement with the 129/Sv paper rests on; the sentence names no strain.
+ 1 more reference
As with the Dnd1 row, the targeted gene is named in the genotype and not bound, for the same reason.

description: >-
  The commonest tumour of the newborn, and a germ cell tumour in a place with no gonad. It is thought
  to arise when a primordial germ cell migrating from the yolk sac to the gonadal ridge is left behind
  in the caudal midline and is reprogrammed to a pluripotent state, after which it differentiates into
  all three germ layers at once. Most are mature, and complete resection with clear margins is the treatment; about one child in ten
  recurs.
  Three things make it dangerous. Before birth, a large solid tumour steals so much cardiac output
  that the fetus goes into high-output failure and hydrops, which is what the prenatal predictors
  are for. In the first weeks after birth, bleeding, into the tumour or at its removal, was the
  commonest cause of death in a Dutch series. And a mature-looking tumour can recur as a yolk sac
  tumour years later, which is what the alpha-fetoprotein surveillance is for.
pathophysiology:
- name: Primordial Germ Cell Left in the Caudal Midline
  role: trigger
  biological_scale: CELLULAR
  description: >-
    A germ cell that does not complete the migration from the yolk sac to the gonadal ridge. The
    midline distribution of extragonadal germ cell tumours is the main evidence for this: the tumours
    appear where the migration route runs.

  - reference: PMID:33906346
    reference_title: >-

    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      SCT is the most common type I GCT and is believed to originate through epigenetic
      reprogramming of early primordial germ cells migrating from the yolk sac to the gonadal
      ridges.
    explanation: >-
      Names the cell and the route this node binds, and keeps the hedge: believed to originate. The
      second half of the sentence is the next node.
  notes: >-
    The other accounts of this tumour's origin in the wider literature name Hensen's node, the
    primitive streak, the caudal cell mass or a totipotent cell. Four sources cited here touch
    on the origin without naming a germ cell, and without data of their own for it. Two series
    do so in their introductions, citing earlier work: one says that teratomas found around
    birth mostly originate from Hensen's node in the sacrococcygeal region or from caudal
    pluripotent primitive stem cells; the other attributes the site to the many pluripotent
    cells occurring in this area, without saying what those cells are. A systematic review of
    fetus in fetu says in its discussion that teratomas are neoplasms originating from embryonic
    pluripotent cells, and a review of caudal cell mass anomalies lists sacrococcygeal teratoma
    among the forms that anomalous development of the caudal cell mass can take, describing that
    mass as a remnant of the embryologic primitive streak composed of undifferentiated
    pluripotential cells. This entry records the germ cell account because two cited reviews
    make it, one of them with the argument from where these tumours occur, and not because the
    alternatives were weighed and rejected. HPO takes the other view: its text definition of
    HP:0030736, the term this entry binds for the mass, says these tumours arise from totipotent
    cells from the node of Hensen. Nothing cited here gives evidence on that, and the entry does
    not adjudicate it. The label on GO:0008354 is the committed cache's, germ cell migration.
    The current ontology makes that an exact synonym and gives the canonical label as primordial
    germ cell migration. Two other entries in kb/ carry the same stale string, so this is
    corpus-wide cache drift rather than a binding error here; refreshing it belongs in its own
    pass.

- name: Malignant Yolk Sac Component
  role: effector
  biological_scale: CELLULAR
  description: >-
    Yolk sac tumour, the malignant histology this tumour recurs as. Microscopic foci of it inside an
    otherwise mature teratoma raise the recurrence rate sharply, which is the practical reason the
    whole specimen is examined rather than sampled.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:39016163
    reference_title: >-

      teratoma.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      We identified 56 patients with mature SCT, of which 9 (16%) demonstrated microscopic YST.
    explanation: >-
      How often the microscopic component is present in tumours called mature, in a
      single-institution series.
  - reference: PMID:39016163
    reference_title: >-
      Impact of microscopic deposits of yolk sac tumor on recurrence of mature sacrococcygeal
      teratoma.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Recurrence was more likely in patients with microscopic YST [5/9 (56%) vs. 2/47 (4%), p =
      0.021] and positive margins [6/24 (35%) vs. 1/32 (3.1%), p = 0.030].
    explanation: >-
      What it does to the recurrence rate, with the margin status beside it. Nine patients in the
      exposed arm, so read it as a signal rather than a rate.

      evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
      snippet: >-

  - target: Malignant recurrence
    causal_link_type: DIRECT
    description: >-

- name: Pelvic and Perineal Mass Effect
  role: effector
  biological_scale: ORGANISM
  description: >-
    The consequences that outlast the tumour. In the Dutch national questionnaire study of long-term

    unacceptable scar. Its authors conclude that clinical variables cannot clearly identify the
    patients at higher risk; on univariate analysis the one variable its abstract reports as a risk
    factor for any of them is tumour size above 500 cm3, for the scar. A single-centre series'
    review of the literature reports that the complications listed in one passage, early and late
    and mostly obstructive and bowel problems, are commoner in tumours with a larger intrapelvic
    component; that passage does not list incontinence or the scar; the series' introduction names
    incontinence and aesthetic concerns among long-term complications without tying them to the
    intrapelvic part.

- name: Pelvic and Sacral Nerve Injury
  role: effector
  biological_scale: TISSUE
  description: >-
    Injury to the pelvic and sacral nerves. A 2022 MRI series restates tumour compression or
    infiltration of the sacral nerves among the tumour's complications, and a 1990 series attributes
    leg weakness to sciatic nerve palsy without saying what caused the palsy. The operation as a
    second cause is the entry's inference: none of the sources cited on this node names a surgical
    nerve injury, and the 2020 series' surgical injury is to the pelvic organs. The other cited
    sources give associations rather than a measured mechanism: functional sequelae were commoner
    after resecting large intrapelvic tumours by an abdominoperineal approach (67% in the 1990
    series); in a 2020 single-centre series the patients with functional disorders had a low
    1-minute Apgar score, larger tumours needing abdominosacral resection, surgical injury to the
    pelvic organs and immature or malignant histology; and a 2023 systematic review associates
    higher Altman type, unfavourable tumour biology and reoperation with poor function. The Dutch
    national questionnaire study found neither Altman type nor histopathology to be a risk factor
    for any long-term sequela.
  evidence:

    reference_title: >-

    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-

phenotypes:
- category: Neoplasm
  name: Sacrococcygeal mass
  frequency: OBLIGATE
  phenotype_term:
    preferred_term: congenital mass at the sacrococcyx
    term:
      id: HP:0030736
      label: Sacrococcygeal teratoma
  description: >-
    The defining finding, found before birth in half to nearly three quarters of cases in
    population-based series. The sacrococcygeal region is where most infant teratomas arise.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:16420341
    reference_title: >-
      Descriptive epidemiology of teratoma in infants, Hawaii, 1986-2001.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      A total of 22 cases were identified among deliveries in 1986-2001, of which 13 (59.1%) were
      located in the sacrococcygeal region.
    explanation: >-
      Nearly three fifths of all infant teratomas in a population-based Hawaii registry were at this
      site, which is the fact that makes this the default teratoma of the newborn.
  - reference: PMID:23432104
    reference_title: >-
      High prevalence of sacrococcygeal teratoma in Finland - a nationwide population-based study.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Tumours were detected in utero in 55% of the pregnancies with SCT.
    explanation: >-
      Within the range: 55% of pregnancies in the Finnish national register.
  - reference: PMID:26454470
    reference_title: >-
      Sacrococcygeal teratoma: A population-based study of incidence and prenatal prognostic
      factors.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      A prenatal diagnosis was made in 74% of cases
    explanation: >-
      The top of the range: 74% in a southern Swedish series.
  - reference: PMID:18973151
    reference_title: >-
      Sacrococcygeal teratoma over two decades: birth prevalence, prenatal diagnosis and clinical
      outcomes.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      There was a prenatal diagnosis in 50% of cases.
    explanation: >-
      The bottom of the range: 50% in a regional database.
- category: Prenatal
  name: Hydrops fetalis
  phenotype_term:
    preferred_term: fetal hydrops
    term:
      id: HP:0001789
      label: Hydrops fetalis
  description: >-
    The decompensated end of the high-output state, and a strong reported predictor of poor outcome at
    an odds ratio of 21 in one cohort - though a cited growth-velocity study reports a higher odds
    ratio for a different measure, and one cited review finds no survival effect for hydrops at all,
    which the entry records as an open disagreement rather than resolving.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:34327722
    reference_title: >-
      Factors associated with poor outcome in fetuses prenatally diagnosed with sacrococcygeal
      teratoma.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Potential risk factors for poor outcome were the presence of fetal hydrops (OR: 21.0, CI:
      2.6-275.1, p = 0.012) and cardiomegaly (OR: 10.3, CI: 1.9-55.8, p = 0.011).
    explanation: >-
      The odds ratio and its confidence interval, which spans two orders of magnitude.
  - reference: PMID:38731178
    reference_title: >-
      Perinatal Outcomes of Intrauterine Interventions for Fetal Sacrococcygeal Teratoma Based on
      Different Surgical Techniques-A Systematic Review.
    supports: REFUTE
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      In our evaluation, we determined that the presence of fetal hydrops and cardiac failure had no
      significant impact on survival in SCT cases.
    explanation: >-
      The opposite finding, from a review of 157 fetuses across three management groups - 16, 48 and 93, a sum the abstract does not
      itself state. REFUTE
      against the claim that hydrops predicts survival, and the reason this entry carries a
      controversy discussion rather than a single prognostic statement.
- category: Prenatal
  name: Cardiomegaly
  phenotype_term:
    preferred_term: fetal cardiomegaly
    term:
      id: HP:0001640
      label: Cardiomegaly
  description: >-
    The heart enlarging under a sustained output demand, and one of the two potential risk factors
    for poor outcome that an 84-fetus Dutch national cohort identifies. Its abstract reports no
    multivariate analysis; the three-centre series that ran one found no factor independent, while
    two growth series each found one growth measure that was.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:34327722
    reference_title: >-
      Factors associated with poor outcome in fetuses prenatally diagnosed with sacrococcygeal
      teratoma.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Potential risk factors for poor outcome were fetal hydrops and cardiomegaly.
    explanation: >-
      The authors' own summary of their analysis, which ran on the 68 fetuses left after sixteen
      terminations were excluded.
- category: Prenatal
  name: Polyhydramnios
  phenotype_term:
    preferred_term: polyhydramnios
    term:
      id: HP:0001561
      label: Polyhydramnios
  description: >-
    Excess amniotic fluid, much commoner among the fetuses who did not survive in the non-intervention arm of one review, and a component of one proposed composite index.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:39753205
    reference_title: >-
      Proposal of a novel index in assessing perinatal mortality in prenatal diagnosis of
      Sacrococcygeal teratoma.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: INDIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      A cutoff value of THC plus polyhydramnios higher than 3.0 was associated with postnatal
      mortality with 100 % sensitivity and 86 % specificity.
    explanation: >-
      The composite index this phenotype enters, with its reported accuracy. Eleven fetuses in that
      series, and 100% sensitivity on a denominator that small is a property of the sample.
- category: Prenatal
  name: Premature birth
  phenotype_term:
    preferred_term: preterm delivery
    term:
      id: HP:0001622
      label: Premature birth
  description: >-
    Earlier delivery is associated with death in every management group of one review, and is named
    with intrauterine death as a complication of minimally invasive fetal therapy. Early delivery is
    also part of management: at one centre, eleven fetuses showing impending fetal or maternal
    decompensation were delivered early and nine survived, with no death attributed to prematurity,
    and a hydropic fetus delivered at 27 weeks for maternal mirror syndrome survived resection. In a
    Dutch series prematurity was a risk factor for death from haemorrhage after birth.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:24488859
    reference_title: >-
      Minimally invasive therapy for fetal sacrococcygeal teratoma: case series and systematic
      review of the literature.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      The other three cases resulted in preterm labor within 10 days of surgery.
    explanation: >-
      Preterm labour as a consequence of the intervention rather than of the disease, in three of
      five treated fetuses.
  - reference: PMID:29734172
    reference_title: >-
      Preemptive Delivery and Immediate Resection for Fetuses with High-Risk Sacrococcygeal
      Teratomas.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Forty-two SCT fetuses were evaluated, and 11 were preemptively delivered in response to
      impending fetal or maternal decompensation. Nine (81.8%) survived.
    explanation: >-
      Early delivery of eleven fetuses with impending fetal or maternal decompensation at one
      centre, and their survival.
  - reference: PMID:29734172
    reference_title: >-
      Preemptive Delivery and Immediate Resection for Fetuses with High-Risk Sacrococcygeal
      Teratomas.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      There were no deaths related to prematurity in this cohort.
    explanation: >-
      No death attributed to prematurity among those delivered early.
  - reference: PMID:27502009
    reference_title: >-
      Hemorrhage is the most common cause of neonatal mortality in patients with sacrococcygeal
      teratoma.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Risk factors for hemorrhagic mortality were prematurity, tumor volume>1000cm3 and performance
      of an emergency operation.
    explanation: >-
      Prematurity as a risk factor for death from haemorrhage after birth.
  - reference: PMID:18675620
    reference_title: >-
      Survival of a profoundly hydropic fetus with a sacrococcygeal teratoma delivered at 27 weeks
      of gestation for maternal mirror syndrome.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      We now report successful postpartum resection and survival of a hydropic fetus delivered at 27
      weeks for maternal mirror syndrome that may assist in counseling families in similar
      situations.
    explanation: >-
      A hydropic fetus delivered at 27 weeks for maternal mirror syndrome, who survived resection.
- category: Biochemical
  name: Elevated serum alpha-fetoprotein
  phenotype_term:
    preferred_term: elevated serum alpha-fetoprotein
    term:
      id: HP:0006254
      label: Elevated circulating alpha-fetoprotein concentration
  description: >-
    The marker of the malignant component, and the basis of surveillance. Interpreting it in an infant is the hard part: alpha-fetoprotein is enormous at birth and halves every five days through the first four weeks, then
    settles: between day 180 and day 720 the cited reference study reports no further decline, and
    adult levels are still not reached by two years.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:32376010
    reference_title: >-
      Diagnostic accuracy of serum alpha-fetoprotein levels in diagnosing recurrent sacrococcygeal
      teratoma: A systematic review.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Fifteen studies (613 patients, 121 recurrences) were included and these mainly described serum
      AFP levels in patients with recurrent SCT (n = 111); 83 (75%) patients with recurrent SCT had
      elevated serum AFP levels.
    explanation: >-
      The included studies, with 121 recurrences in all, describe the serum level in 111 patients
      with a recurrence; 83 of them (75%) had an elevated marker. The authors' own caveat, quoted on
      the surveillance row and the readout, is that levels are mainly reported in patients with
      raised levels or at recurrence, so the sensitivity to detect recurrence could be
      overestimated.
  - reference: PMID:9592840
    reference_title: >-
      Alpha 1-fetoprotein (AFP) reference values in infants up to 2 years of age.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: INDIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      At birth mean serum AFP levels were 41,687 ng/ml in 256 term babies and 158,125 ng/ml in 90
      premature babies born before the 37th gestational week, excluding samples from children with
      factors known to be associated with AFP elevation.

      disease.

- category: Dermatological
  name: Cosmetically unacceptable surgical scar
  frequency: FREQUENT
  phenotype_term:
    preferred_term: cosmetically unacceptable scar after resection
    term:
      id: HP:0100699
      label: Scarring
  description: >-
    Two of every five respondents in the Dutch national study rated the scar cosmetically
    unacceptable. That is the highest single complaint the study reports, although a larger share,
    46 percent, reported impaired bowel function or urinary incontinence as a composite. It is a
    consequence of the resection rather than of the tumour, which is why it is wired from the
    mass-effect node and not from the mass itself, and it is recorded because the same study found
    it affects quality of life.
  notes: >-
    Scarring is the general, site-unspecified HPO term. An OLS search of HPO for l~scar returns a
    dozen terms, every other one of them anatomically specific - macular, corneal, chorioretinal,
    atrophic, cigarette-paper - so none of them is narrower in the sense this row needs. Every
    resected patient has a scar; what the source measures is the proportion who find it
    unacceptable, and HPO has no term for that, so the preferred term carries it.
  evidence:

- category: Prenatal
  name: Placentomegaly
  phenotype_term:
    preferred_term: placentomegaly
    term:
      id: HP:0006267
      label: Large placenta
  description: >-
    An enlarged placenta, which the cited meta-analysis groups with cardiomegaly and fetal hydrops
    as a factor associated with cardiac failure. That is why it sits beside hydrops under the
    high-output node rather than as an independent lesion. The review gives no frequency, so this
    row carries none, and it reports association without direction, so the edge is drawn through
    unknown intermediates. In one case of mirror syndrome it appeared with right heart failure and
    polyhydramnios before overt hydrops, and in another the placenta was grossly oedematous, at
    1,280 g, with marked hydropic change of the villi.

- category: Prenatal
  name: Maternal mirror syndrome
  phenotype_term:
    preferred_term: maternal mirror syndrome
  description: >-
    A preeclampsia-like illness in the mother, defined by fetal hydrops with placental and maternal
    oedema. In one case it began shortly after the fetus showed right heart failure, placentomegaly
    and polyhydramnios, before overt hydrops, which the authors set against the syndrome's usual
    association with severe fetal hydrops, and it resolved after delivery. A review of the tumour's
    management names it among the potentially lethal conditions a tumour can precipitate; with fetal
    hydrops it carries a grave prognosis, and it can force delivery.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:30949371
    reference_title: >-
      Significant Clinical Manifestations in Ballantyne Syndrome, after a Case Report and Literature
      Review: Recognizing Preeclampsia as a Differential Diagnosis.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: BACKGROUND
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Ballantyne syndrome (BS) also called mirror syndrome or triple edema is defined by the
      presence of a clinical triad that includes fetal hydrops and placental and maternal edema [ 1
      ].
    explanation: >-
      The syndrome's defining triad, stated with a citation to other work.
  - reference: PMID:30949371
    reference_title: >-

    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL

    explanation: >-

      snippet: >-
        We now report successful postpartum resection and survival of a hydropic fetus delivered at
        27 weeks for maternal mirror syndrome that may assist in counseling families in similar
        situations.
      explanation: >-
        A delivery at 27 weeks made for maternal mirror syndrome, and the infant's survival after
        resection.
  notes: >-
    No ontology term is bound. OLS searches of HP and MONDO on 20 Nov 2026 found nothing for
    "Ballantyne syndrome" or "maternal mirror"; for "mirror syndrome", HP returns Mirror image
    polydactyly and Heterotaxy, and MONDO returns mirror polydactyly and limb-duplication syndromes,
    dextrocardia with situs inversus and TUBB3-related tubulinopathy, none of them the maternal
    syndrome. The row records a condition of the mother, which the cited sources report in
    pregnancies with this tumour.
- category: Neonatal
  name: Neonatal death
  phenotype_term:
    preferred_term: neonatal death
  description: >-
    Death in the first weeks after birth. In a Dutch series of 235 children treated from 1970 to
    2010, nine (3.8%) died within 27 days of birth, six of them within two days; tumour haemorrhage,
    circulatory failure or both were related to seven of these deaths, and haemorrhagic deaths made
    up almost 70% of the neonatal mortality.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:27502009
    reference_title: >-
      Hemorrhage is the most common cause of neonatal mortality in patients with sacrococcygeal
      teratoma.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Nine others (3.8%) died postnatally (age 1-27days), six even within two days after birth. In
      seven of these nine patients death was related to tumor-hemorrhage and/or circulatory failure.
    explanation: >-
      The nine neonatal deaths and the share related to tumour haemorrhage, circulatory failure or
      both.
  - reference: PMID:27502009
    reference_title: >-
      Hemorrhage is the most common cause of neonatal mortality in patients with sacrococcygeal
      teratoma.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Hemorrhagic mortality of neonates with SCT is relatively high (3.8%) representing almost 70%
      of the overall mortality in the neonatal period.
    explanation: >-
      Haemorrhagic deaths as almost 70% of the neonatal mortality.
  notes: >-
    No term is bound, as for the stillbirth row. HP:0003811 Neonatal death exists, but an OLS
    ancestor walk returns only All, Age of death, Clinical modifier, Clinical course and
    Mortality/Aging - no HP:0000118 Phenotypic abnormality - so it is outside the PhenotypeTerm enum
    and the term validator rejects it here.
genetic:
- name: BAK1 rs210138
  gene_term:
    preferred_term: BAK1
    term:
      id: hgnc:949
      label: BAK1
  relationship_type: SUSCEPTIBILITY
  notes: >-
    A susceptibility allele first found for adult testicular germ cell tumour and then associated with
    paediatric germ cell tumours in two independent designs. Neither study is of sacrococcygeal
    teratoma specifically: both pool germ cell tumours across sites, and this entry records the allele
    at that level rather than claiming it for this tumour.
  evidence:
