  - reference: PMID:22072546
    reference_title: >-
      Associations between variants in KITLG, SPRY4, BAK1, and DMRT1 and pediatric germ cell tumors.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: INDIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      We observed a significant association for rs210138 (BAK1) and pediatric GCT overall (odds
      ratio (OR) = 1.80, 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.10-2.95, P = 0.02) with non-significant
      associations similar in magnitude in both the pediatric (P = 0.09) and adolescent (P = 0.06)
      age groups.
    explanation: >-
      The association in 52 paediatric germ cell tumours against 141 newborn blood-spot controls.
      Small, and significant overall while neither age stratum reaches significance on its own.
  - reference: PMID:28295819
    reference_title: >-
      Variants in BAK1, SPRY4, and GAB2 are associated with pediatric germ cell tumors: A report
      from the children's oncology group.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: INDIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      A variant in BAK1 (rs210138) was positively associated with GCT (OR [95% CI]: 1.70 [1.32,
      2.18])
    explanation: >-
      The same variant in a case-parent triad design with 366 complete trios, which does not share
      the control group of the study above. The same sentence continues with a stronger estimated
      effect for testis tumours, which is where this locus was first found.
- name: SPRY4
  gene_term:
    preferred_term: SPRY4
    term:
      id: hgnc:15533
      label: SPRY4
  relationship_type: SUSCEPTIBILITY
  notes: >-
    The two cited studies report this gene in opposite directions - risk in one, protection in the
    other - at different variants. Recorded as susceptibility and not as a direction.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:28295819
    reference_title: >-
      Variants in BAK1, SPRY4, and GAB2 are associated with pediatric germ cell tumors: A report
      from the children's oncology group.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: INDIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      A variant in SPRY4 (rs4624820) was associated with reduced risk of GCT (OR [95% CI]: 0.70
      [0.57, 0.86]).
    explanation: >-
      A protective association at rs4624820 in the triad study.
  - reference: PMID:22072546
    reference_title: >-
      Associations between variants in KITLG, SPRY4, BAK1, and DMRT1 and pediatric germ cell tumors.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: INDIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      The KITLG (rs4474514) and SPRY4 (rs4324715) variants were significantly associated with GCT
      only in the adolescent age group (rs4474514: OR = 2.28, 95% CI 1.09-4.79, P = 0.03 and
      rs4324715: OR = 2.40, 95% CI 1.19-4.83, P = 0.01).
    explanation: >-
      A risk association at a different variant, rs4324715, and only in adolescents. Different
      variant and different stratum from the sentence above, which is why the two are not in
      conflict and why no direction is asserted.
- name: GAB2 rs948662
  gene_term:
    preferred_term: GAB2
    term:
      id: hgnc:14458
      label: GAB2
  relationship_type: SUSCEPTIBILITY
  notes: >-
    Reported in one of the two cited association studies and not tested in the other.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:28295819
    reference_title: >-
      Variants in BAK1, SPRY4, and GAB2 are associated with pediatric germ cell tumors: A report
      from the children's oncology group.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: INDIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Finally, a SNP in GAB2 (rs948662) was associated with increased risk for GCT (OR [95% CI]:
      1.56 [1.20, 2.03]).
    explanation: >-
      The association, in 366 complete trios.
- name: KITLG rs4474514
  gene_term:
    preferred_term: KITLG
    term:
      id: hgnc:6343
      label: KITLG
  relationship_type: SUSCEPTIBILITY
  notes: >-
    Associated in adolescents in one study, and in the other as a maternal effect - the mother's
    genotype rather than the child's - which is a different claim from an association with the
    child's own genotype. The same study reports a separate paternal parent-of-origin effect at an
    unrelated locus, which it labels as such and which it does not label this one.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:28295819
    reference_title: >-
      Variants in BAK1, SPRY4, and GAB2 are associated with pediatric germ cell tumors: A report
      from the children's oncology group.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: INDIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      A maternal effect was observed for KITLG SNP rs4474514 (OR [95% CI]: 1.66 [1.21, 2.28])
    explanation: >-
      The maternal effect at this variant: the mother's genotype rather than the child's. The same
      sentence goes on to report a paternal parent-of-origin effect at an unrelated locus.
animal_models:
- name: Dnd1 mutant 129/Sv mouse (Ter)
  species: Mouse
  genotype: Dnd1 Ter (R178*) premature stop codon on the 129 background
  publication: PMID:29378702
  description: >-
    The classical teratoma mouse. Loss of DND1 drastically raises teratoma incidence, and the
    mechanism is worked out: DND1 suppresses a microRNA that inhibits EZH2, so its loss lowers
    H3K27me3 at a cell-cycle gene and the germ cells reprogramme.
  notes: >-
    The targeted gene is named in the genotype and not bound. A model organism's own gene takes its
    model-organism database identifier, not the human HGNC one, and no MGI identifier for mouse Dnd1
    could be resolved from any source available here: there is no local MGI build and the Alliance
    search endpoint returned nothing. Binding the human gene instead would put a mouse knockout on
    the human gene's page, which is the thing that rule exists to prevent.
  modeled_mechanisms:
  - target: Epigenetic Reprogramming to a Pluripotent State
    relationship: RECAPITULATES
    fidelity: MODERATE
    model_scale: MOLECULAR
    description: >-
      The only cited source that shows the reprogramming step happening, with a named chromatin
      mechanism and both a loss-of-function and a rescue arm.
    limitations: >-
      The tumours are testicular, not sacrococcygeal, and they arise in one inbred strain. No cited
      source reports a sacrococcygeal teratoma model in any species, so the step this link supplies is
      transferred across both organ and genetic background.
    divergences:
    - divergence_type: BOUNDARY_OMISSION
      materiality: QUALIFYING
      description: >-
        The model contains the gonad; this disease's defining feature is a germ cell that never
        reached one. Nothing in the model represents the caudal midline.
    - divergence_type: SPECIES_MISMATCH
      materiality: QUALIFYING
      description: >-
        No DND1 variant is reported in human sacrococcygeal teratoma by any cited source, and the Ter
        allele's effect is confined to the 129 strain background.
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:29378702
      reference_title: >-
        Dnd1-mediated epigenetic control of teratoma formation in mouse.
      supports: SUPPORT
      directness: DIRECT
      quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
      evidence_source: MODEL_ORGANISM
      snippet: >-
        Mutation of the dead-end 1 (Dnd1) gene, which encodes an RNA-binding protein, drastically
        enhances teratoma formation in the 129/Sv mouse strain.
      explanation: >-
        What the model does, and the strain dependence that is one of its two recorded
        divergences.
    - reference: PMID:29378702
      reference_title: >-
        Dnd1-mediated epigenetic control of teratoma formation in mouse.
      supports: SUPPORT
      directness: DIRECT
      quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
      evidence_source: MODEL_ORGANISM
      snippet: >-
        These results revealed an epigenetic molecular linkage between Dnd1 and the suppression of
        testicular teratoma formation.
      explanation: >-
        The authors' own statement of what they showed, with the organ in it: testicular.
- name: MC4R G25S congenital mouse strains
  species: Mouse
  genotype: LT-MC4R G25S point mutation, alone and with the Dnd1 Ter allele
  publication: PMID:33568756
  description: >-
    A second teratoma locus, mapped and then edited. It is recorded here mainly for what it got
    wrong: the strains make teratomas, but in the wrong organ.
  notes: >-
    As with the Dnd1 row, the targeted gene is named in the genotype and not bound, for the same
    reason.
  modeled_mechanisms:
  - target: Epigenetic Reprogramming to a Pluripotent State
    relationship: PARTIALLY_RECAPITULATES
    fidelity: LOW
    model_scale: ORGANISM
    description: >-
      These strains do form germ cell teratomas, so they reach the node; they reach it in the wrong
      organ. Four of them gave ovarian teratomas where testicular ones were expected, and the
      authors call that result surprising. The paper also states, as background, that Dnd1-mutant
      mice show germ cell loss rather than teratoma, which reads against the other cited mouse paper
      reporting that Dnd1 mutation enhances teratoma formation in 129/Sv. The strain behind the germ
      cell loss sentence is not given in the cached abstract, so this entry cannot say whether the
      two results are a genuine disagreement or two strains behaving differently.
    limitations: >-
      Neither result is in the caudal midline and neither is in a human, so the site this disease is
      defined by is outside the model. The organ the strain was built for is not the organ it
      produced.
    divergences:
    - divergence_type: BOUNDARY_OMISSION
      materiality: QUALIFYING
      description: >-
        The caudal midline is not in the model. Every teratoma these strains produce is gonadal,
        where this disease is extragonadal and sacrococcygeal, so the anatomical site and the
        tissues around it are outside the model's boundary.
    - divergence_type: SPECIES_MISMATCH
      materiality: QUALIFYING
      description: >-
        Mouse germ cell teratoma is strain-restricted in a way human sacrococcygeal teratoma is not,
        and the strain backgrounds carrying these alleles have no human counterpart.
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:33568756
      reference_title: >-
        MC4R mutant mice develop ovarian teratomas.
      supports: SUPPORT
      directness: DIRECT
      quote_role: BACKGROUND
      evidence_source: MODEL_ORGANISM
      snippet: >-
        However, the phenotype of mice with a mutated Dnd1 gene was germ cell loss.
      explanation: >-
        The germ cell loss result, stated by the authors as background. Quoted here because it is
        what the apparent disagreement with the 129/Sv paper rests on; the sentence names no strain.
    - reference: PMID:33568756
      reference_title: >-
        MC4R mutant mice develop ovarian teratomas.
      supports: SUPPORT
      directness: DIRECT
      quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
      evidence_source: MODEL_ORGANISM
      snippet: >-
        Surprisingly, highly developed ovarian teratomas (OTs), instead of testicular teratomas,
        appeared not only in the LT-Ter-MC4RG25S and LT-MC4RG25S strains but also in the LT-ett1
        and LT-Ter-ett1 strains.
      explanation: >-
        The wrong-organ result, with the authors' own word for it. Four strains, all giving ovarian
        teratomas, which is what the BOUNDARY_OMISSION divergence records.
biochemical:
- name: Serum alpha-fetoprotein
  biomarker_term:
    preferred_term: alpha-fetoprotein
    term:
      id: NCIT:C16278
      label: Alpha-Fetoprotein
  loinc_term:
    id: LOINC:1834-1
    label: Alpha-1-Fetoprotein [Mass/volume] in Serum or Plasma
  presence: >-
    Physiologically high at birth and falling over the first months of life; raised for the child's
    age, or rising, with a malignant yolk sac component
  notes: >-
    A value in this disease is read against the child's age (PMID:42460113). The reference figures
    are population figures and are given here, with their evidence, rather than as reference ranges:
    at birth the reference interval is 15.7 to 146.5 ug/mL, and at discharge from the nursery, 60
    +/- 24 hours after birth, 9.7 to 111.9 ug/mL, in 260 term and near-term newborns
    (PMID:15469851); between day 180 and day 720 the upper limit is 87 ng/mL, and adult levels (0 to
    6 ng/mL) are not reached by two years (PMID:9592840). The record's one reference range is the
    Dutch recurrence cut-off, which this disease owns. After resection in a newborn the level keeps
    falling for months, nine on average in one small series, which should not be read as a relapse
    (PMID:16621769). Whether the decline after resection differs in children who recur is contested:
    a series of 55 newborns without recurrence found the half-life lengthening with age, with a
    formula for recurrent tumours that rises more steeply with age (PMID:30249359), while the Dutch
    nationwide cohort found no difference in the dynamics after resection between children who did
    and did not recur (PMID:38418277). The Dutch cut-off of 55 ug/L is below the 87 ng/mL upper
    limit for infants aged 180 to 720 days, and the Dutch abstract gives the cut-off without an age
    stratum. 1 ug/mL is 1,000 ng/mL; ng/mL and ug/L are the same.
  reference_ranges:
  - loinc_term:
      id: LOINC:1834-1
      label: Alpha-1-Fetoprotein [Mass/volume] in Serum or Plasma
    population: >-
      Children followed after resection of a sacrococcygeal teratoma, Dutch nationwide cohort of 57
      patients treated 1980 to 2018
    notes: >-
      The cohort gives no normal interval; the bands are its recurrence cut-off, which the source
      words as exceeding 55 ug/L.
    interpretation_bands:
    - name: Below the recurrence cut-off
      upper_bound: 55
      unit: ug/L
      interpretation: >-
        Does not rule out recurrence: in the same cohort the level did not predict mature or
        immature recurrence, and the cut-off's sensitivity was 50%.
    - name: Above the recurrence cut-off
      lower_bound: 55
      unit: ug/L
      abnormal_flag: HIGH
      interpretation: >-
        Predictive of recurrence in this cohort, with a sensitivity of 50% and a specificity of 100%
        (area under the curve 0.636); the authors add that values above it can indicate malignant
        recurrence especially.
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:38418277
      reference_title: >-
        The Diagnostic Accuracy of Serum Alpha-Fetoprotein Levels in Follow-up for Recurrence of
        Sacrococcygeal Teratoma; a Nationwide Review of SCT Cases in the Netherlands.
      supports: SUPPORT
      directness: DIRECT
      quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
      evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
      snippet: >-
        A cut-off value of 55 μg/L was found to be predictive for recurrent SCT with an Area Under
        the Curve (AUC) of 0.636 with sensitivity of 50% and specificity of 100%.
      explanation: >-
        The cut-off and its accuracy, in a cohort of 57 children with 20 recurrences.
    - reference: PMID:38418277
      reference_title: >-
        The Diagnostic Accuracy of Serum Alpha-Fetoprotein Levels in Follow-up for Recurrence of
        Sacrococcygeal Teratoma; a Nationwide Review of SCT Cases in the Netherlands.
      supports: SUPPORT
      directness: DIRECT
      quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
      evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
      snippet: >-
        However, serum AFP levels exceeding 55 μg/L can indicate recurrent SCT, especially malignant
        recurrences.
      explanation: >-
        The authors' reading of the cut-off, and its wording.
  readouts:
  - target: Malignant Yolk Sac Component
    relationship: READOUT_OF
    direction: POSITIVE
    endpoint_context: MONITORING
    interpretation: >-
      In follow-up for recurrence, a readout of the malignant yolk sac component. In a systematic
      review its sensitivity for malignant recurrence was 96%; the review cautions that its
      sensitivity to detect recurrence could be overestimated, because levels are mainly reported in
      patients with raised levels or at recurrence. In the Dutch cohort the level rose in malignant
      recurrences but did not predict mature or immature recurrence, and a normal value did not rule
      recurrence out.
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:32376010
      reference_title: >-
        Diagnostic accuracy of serum alpha-fetoprotein levels in diagnosing recurrent sacrococcygeal
        teratoma: A systematic review.
      supports: SUPPORT
      directness: DIRECT
      quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
      evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
      snippet: >-
        The sensitivity of AFP levels to detect malignant recurrence was 96%.
      explanation: >-
        The sensitivity for malignant recurrence. The review's caveat, given for its sensitivity to
        detect recurrence, is the next item.
    - reference: PMID:32376010
      reference_title: >-
        Diagnostic accuracy of serum alpha-fetoprotein levels in diagnosing recurrent sacrococcygeal
        teratoma: A systematic review.
      supports: SUPPORT
      directness: INDIRECT
      quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
      evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
      snippet: >-
        Diagnostic accuracy of serum AFP levels to detect recurrent SCT seems promising, though
        sensitivity could be overestimated since serum AFP levels are mainly described in patients
        with elevated AFP levels or at recurrent SCT.
      explanation: >-
        The review's caveat on its sensitivity to detect recurrence. Indirect: the review gives it
        for recurrence in general, not for malignant recurrence, so it bears on this readout of the
        malignant component only by inference.
    - reference: PMID:38418277
      reference_title: >-
        The Diagnostic Accuracy of Serum Alpha-Fetoprotein Levels in Follow-up for Recurrence of
        Sacrococcygeal Teratoma; a Nationwide Review of SCT Cases in the Netherlands.
      supports: SUPPORT
      directness: DIRECT
      quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
      evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
      snippet: >-
        However, serum AFP levels did significantly increase in malignant recurrences (n = 7) (p =
        0.03) compared to patients without recurrence.
      explanation: >-
        The rise in malignant recurrence, seven malignant recurrences.
    - reference: PMID:38418277
      reference_title: >-
        The Diagnostic Accuracy of Serum Alpha-Fetoprotein Levels in Follow-up for Recurrence of
        Sacrococcygeal Teratoma; a Nationwide Review of SCT Cases in the Netherlands.
      supports: SUPPORT
      directness: DIRECT
      quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
      evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
      snippet: >-
        Serum AFP levels are not predictive for mature or immature recurrent SCT and normal AFP
        levels do not rule out recurrent SCT.
      explanation: >-
        The other side of the readout: in the Dutch cohort the level did not predict mature or
        immature recurrence, and a normal value did not rule recurrence out.
    - reference: PMID:7508500
      reference_title: "Malignant benign neonatal sacrococcygeal teratoma."
      supports: SUPPORT
      directness: DIRECT
      quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
      evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
      snippet: >-
        The malignant recurrence (all originally reported as being mature benign SCT) appeared at
        20.3 +/- 1.5 months and had markedly elevated serum alpha-fetoprotein levels (7,320 +/-
        4,630 micrograms/L).
      explanation: >-
        How high the level ran in the malignant recurrences of one series of 36 children, after
        tumours first reported as mature. The abstract reports six recurrences, three of them
        benign, so the mean rests on about three children.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:42460113
    reference_title: >-
      Age-Adjusted AFP Interpretation in Neonatal Sacrococcygeal Teratoma: Why Adult Reference
      Ranges May Mislead.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      In neonatal sacrococcygeal masses, AFP should be interpreted in neonatal context and followed
      serially after resection.
    explanation: >-
      Why the age-specific figures are given: a single value in a newborn is less informative
      against an adult range.
  - reference: PMID:15469851
    reference_title: >-
      Alpha-fetoprotein in the early neonatal period--a large study and review of the literature.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Due to the nonnormal distribution of AFP levels, it is useful to relate to reference interval
      for AFP concentrations at birth that was 15.7-146.5 microg/ml, based on 95% confidence
      interval (CI).
    explanation: >-
      The reference interval at birth, from cord blood of 260 term and near-term newborns of at
      least 34 weeks' gestation and 1700 g.
  - reference: PMID:15469851
    reference_title: >-
      Alpha-fetoprotein in the early neonatal period--a large study and review of the literature.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Upon discharge, AFP concentrations dropped to 9.7-111.9 microg/ml (95% CI) with a median of
      34.2 microg/ml.
    explanation: >-
      The interval at discharge, 60 +/- 24 hours after birth, in the same newborns.
  - reference: PMID:15469851
    reference_title: >-
      Alpha-fetoprotein in the early neonatal period--a large study and review of the literature.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      A significant negative correlation was found between AFP serum levels and gestational age and
      to a lesser extent with birthweight.
    explanation: >-
      The level at birth falls as gestation advances, in newborns of 34 weeks or more, which is why
      one interval does not fit every newborn.
  - reference: PMID:9592840
    reference_title: "Alpha 1-fetoprotein (AFP) reference values in infants up to 2 years of age."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Between day 180 and 720 of life, AFP levels up to 87 ng/ml were within the 95.5% interval
      (assumed logarithmic normal distribution) with a mean of 8 ng/ml without a further decline.
    explanation: >-
      The upper limit between six months and two years, from a study of 524 samples taken between
      birth and two years; the abstract does not say how many fell in this window.
  - reference: PMID:9592840
    reference_title: "Alpha 1-fetoprotein (AFP) reference values in infants up to 2 years of age."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      By the age of 2 years the infants of this study had not reached adult serum AFP levels (0-6
      ng/ml).
    explanation: >-
      Why an adult reference range misleads in a child under two.
  - reference: PMID:16621769
    reference_title: "Alpha-fetoprotein following neonatal resection of sacrococcygeal teratoma."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      AFP has a progressive decrease, which may last 9 months in average and should not be confused
      with tumoral relapse.
    explanation: >-
      The slow fall after resection, in six infants with a prenatally diagnosed tumour.
  - reference: PMID:30249359
    reference_title: "Half-life of alpha-fetoprotein in neonatal sacrococcygeal teratoma."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      The half-life of AFP in neonatal patients with SCT was prolonged in proportion to the age, and
      it was getting longer in recurrent tumor than non-recurrent tumor.
    explanation: >-
      One side of the contested question: in 55 newborns without recurrence the half-life lengthened
      with age, and the abstract's formula for recurrent tumours rises more steeply with age.
  - reference: PMID:38418277
    reference_title: >-
      The Diagnostic Accuracy of Serum Alpha-Fetoprotein Levels in Follow-up for Recurrence of
      Sacrococcygeal Teratoma; a Nationwide Review of SCT Cases in the Netherlands.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      No significant difference was found in serum AFP level dynamics between the recurrence and
      non-recurrence group after initial resection (p = 0.950).
    explanation: >-
      The other side: no difference in the dynamics after resection between children who did and did
      not recur, in the Dutch cohort.
- name: Serum human chorionic gonadotropin
  biomarker_term:
    preferred_term: human chorionic gonadotropin
    term:
      id: NCIT:C2275
      label: Human Chorionic Gonadotropin
  loinc_term:
    id: LOINC:19080-1
    label: Choriogonadotropin [Units/volume] in Serum or Plasma
  presence: >-
    Sometimes measured alongside alpha-fetoprotein in follow-up; raised less often than
    alpha-fetoprotein in one treatment series of malignant germ cell tumours from several sites;
    secretion is reported in one infant's immature teratoma, which also secreted alpha-fetoprotein
    and ACTH
  notes: >-
    The cited sources write beta-hCG and do not name the assay. The record takes LOINC:19080-1, the
    code the Choriocarcinoma entry uses for serum hCG measured in units per volume.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:9834677
    reference_title: >-
      [Importance of long-term follow-up of infants operated of sacro-coccygeal teratoma].
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      The baby must be carefully followed-up and the serum levels of alpha-foetoprotein (a specific
      tumor marker), and sometimes beta-HCG must be regularly measured.
    explanation: >-
      Beta-hCG as an occasional companion to alpha-fetoprotein in follow-up after resection.
  - reference: PMID:1696831
    reference_title: >-
      'JEB'--a carboplatin based regimen for malignant germ cell tumours in children.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: INDIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      AFP levels were elevated in 19, beta-HCG in 8.
    explanation: >-
      Beta-hCG raised in 8 and alpha-fetoprotein in 19 of 21 children with malignant germ cell
      tumours from several sites, four of them sacrococcygeal. Indirect: the abstract does not split
      the markers by site.
  - reference: PMID:26859587
    reference_title: >-
      The first description of metyrapone use in severe Cushing Syndrome due to ectopic ACTH
      secretion in an infant with immature sacrococcygeal teratoma. Case Report.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      We report an 8-month-old female infant with congenital immature sacrococcygeal teratoma
      secreting AFP, beta hCG and ACTH who had undergone non-radical resection of the tumour mass
      and was receiving standard risk chemotherapy (vinblastine, bleomycin, and cisplatin).
    explanation: >-
      A single case of an hCG-secreting immature teratoma, after an incomplete resection.
- name: Maternal serum alpha-fetoprotein and hCG in the second trimester
  presence: Not increased
  context: >-
    The mother's serum at the 15th week of a pregnancy with a fetal sacrococcygeal teratoma
  notes: >-
    Maternal serum alpha-fetoprotein and total beta-hCG matched normal pregnancies in ten
    pregnancies with this tumour, mature and immature or malignant alike, so second-trimester
    maternal serum trisomy screening does not detect it. No biomarker term or LOINC code is bound
    because the source reports the two analytes together, measured in the mother.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:9021828
    reference_title: >-
      Maternal serum alpha-fetoprotein and epithelial tumour marker concentrations are not increased
      by fetal sacrococcygeal teratoma.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Maternal serum alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) and total beta-human chorionic gonadotrophin (hCG)
      concentrations were measured at the 15th gestational week in ten pregnancies complicated by
      fetal sacrococcygeal teratoma. The findings corresponded to those in normal pregnancies.
    explanation: >-
      Neither marker was raised in the mother, in ten pregnancies.
  - reference: PMID:9021828
    reference_title: >-
      Maternal serum alpha-fetoprotein and epithelial tumour marker concentrations are not increased
      by fetal sacrococcygeal teratoma.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Histologically mature and immature/malignant cases did not differ from each other as regards
      the above-mentioned parameters.
    explanation: >-
      No difference between mature and immature or malignant tumours.
  - reference: PMID:9021828
    reference_title: >-
      Maternal serum alpha-fetoprotein and epithelial tumour marker concentrations are not increased
      by fetal sacrococcygeal teratoma.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      This abnormality cannot be detected by maternal serum trisomy screening in the second
      trimester.
    explanation: >-
      The practical consequence for prenatal screening.
diagnosis:
- name: Prenatal ultrasound with tumour volume to fetal weight ratio
  diagnosis_term:
    preferred_term: obstetric ultrasonography
    term:
      id: NCIT:C217447
      label: Diagnostic Obstetric Ultrasound
  description: >-
    The test that finds the tumour and the one the risk stratification is built on. Tumour volume
    divided by estimated fetal weight above 0.12 before 24 weeks is the threshold the field uses; it
    was derived in ten fetuses and validated in a three-centre series that evaluated 79 and excluded
    eleven terminations.
  notes: >-
    The threshold is not settled. The validation study reports 0.12 before 24 weeks with an area
    under the curve of 0.913. A second study reports both 0.12 before 24 weeks and 0.11 before 32
    weeks, so those two are one measure at two gestational windows rather than rival values. A third
    finds that 0.095 predicts poor fetal outcome while 0.12 predicts increased maternal operative
    risk - the same number used for two different questions. Beside them sit a total tumour volume
    over estimated fetal weight of 0.16, a solid tumour volume index of 0.09, a morphology score of
    3, a composite of tumour volume over head circumference plus polyhydramnios at 3.0, growth
    velocity at 7 mm per week, a solid tumour to head volume ratio of 1, a tumour volume over
    biparietal diameter of 60 cm3 per cm, and a volume growth rate above 18.01 cm3 per week and a
    volume above 245 cm3. One cited series finds the solid tumour volume index a better predictor
    than total tumour volume over fetal weight, and another finds no significant difference between
    the ratio and the head-circumference composite; two growth series each report that one growth
    measure alone stayed independent in their own data; no cited source compares all of them. The
    entry records all of them, and the validation study states that none of the factors associated
    with poor prognosis was an independent predictor on multivariate analysis.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:21683219
    reference_title: >-
      Tumor volume to fetal weight ratio as an early prognostic classification for fetal
      sacrococcygeal teratoma.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      A TFR greater than 0.12 predicted poor outcome with 100% sensitivity and 83% specificity.
    explanation: >-
      The original derivation, and its denominator: ten fetuses, five on each side of the threshold.
      A sensitivity of 100% resting on at most five poor outcomes, all above the threshold, is a
      property of the sample.
  - reference: PMID:25783370
    reference_title: >-
      Predictors of poor prognosis in prenatally diagnosed sacrococcygeal teratoma: A
      multiinstitutional review.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      ROC analysis revealed that TFR >0.12 prior to 24 weeks gestation was predictive of poor
      prognosis (AUC=0.913; Sensitivity=91.7%, Specificity=76.2%, PPV=86.8%; NPV=84.2%).
    explanation: >-
      The multi-institutional validation, with the full accuracy figures. It evaluated 79 fetuses
      and excluded eleven terminations, so its analysis rests on at most 68. Sensitivity falls from
      100% to 91.7% and specificity from 83% to 76.2% in a sample several times larger, which is
      what validation usually does.
  - reference: PMID:29495013
    reference_title: >-
      High Tumor Volume to Fetal Weight Ratio Is Associated with Worse Fetal Outcomes and Increased
      Maternal Risk in Fetuses with Sacrococcygeal Teratoma.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      ROC analysis revealed that at <=24 weeks, TFR > 0.095 was predictive of poor fetal outcome and
      TFR > 0.12 was predictive of increased maternal operative risk.
    explanation: >-
      The same ratio splitting into two thresholds for two different outcomes, which is the clearest
      statement in the cited literature that the number is not one number.
  - reference: PMID:39753205
    reference_title: >-
      Proposal of a novel index in assessing perinatal mortality in prenatal diagnosis of
      Sacrococcygeal teratoma.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      There was no significant difference comparing tumor volume to fetal weight ratio (TFR) with
      THC plus polyhydramnios.
    explanation: >-
      One of two direct comparisons of the ratio with another index in the cited literature, the
      other being the solid tumour volume index study in the notes: the ratio against the composite
      of tumour volume over head circumference plus polyhydramnios, with no significant difference,
      in a small series.
  - reference: PMID:39482803
    reference_title: >-
      Growth velocity of fetal sacrococcygeal teratoma as predictor of perinatal morbidity and
      mortality: multicenter study.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      The best predictive cut-off of tumor growth velocity for poor perinatal outcome was 7 mm/week
      (OR, 25.7 (95% CI, 5.6-191.3), P < 0.001), yielding a sensitivity of 88% and a specificity of
      77%.
    explanation: >-
      The competing measure, and the only one that remained an independent factor in its own study's
      stepwise regression. The confidence interval runs from 5.6 to 191.3.
  - reference: PMID:39482803
    reference_title: >-
      Growth velocity of fetal sacrococcygeal teratoma as predictor of perinatal morbidity and
      mortality: multicenter study.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      On stepwise logistic regression analysis, tumor growth velocity was the only remaining
      independent factor associated with poor perinatal outcome
    explanation: >-
      The independence claim itself, which is what makes this measure different in kind from the
      ratio-based measures in this row: every other factor in that regression dropped out.
  - reference: PMID:25783370
    reference_title: >-
      Predictors of poor prognosis in prenatally diagnosed sacrococcygeal teratoma: A
      multiinstitutional review.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      None of the factors associated with poor prognosis were independent predictors on multivariate
      analysis.
    explanation: >-
      The result that qualifies every factor that study found associated with poor prognosis, from
      the study that validated the main one.
- name: Serum alpha-fetoprotein surveillance after resection
  diagnosis_term:
    preferred_term: serum alpha-fetoprotein measurement
    term:
      id: NCIT:C74732
      label: Alpha-fetoprotein Measurement
  measurements:
  - preferred_term: serum alpha-fetoprotein
    term:
      id: LOINC:1834-1
      label: Alpha-1-Fetoprotein [Mass/volume] in Serum or Plasma
  description: >-
    Serial measurement after resection, to catch a malignant recurrence. A systematic review says
    its accuracy for detecting recurrence seems promising, though its sensitivity could be
    overestimated. Reading a single value in an infant is the hard part, because the normal level
    falls steeply through the first weeks and then plateaus above the adult range.
  notes: >-
    The measurement is the LOINC code; the NCIT term carries the action. The newborn and infant
    reference figures and the Dutch recurrence cut-off are on the serum alpha-fetoprotein
    biochemical record.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:32376010
    reference_title: >-
      Diagnostic accuracy of serum alpha-fetoprotein levels in diagnosing recurrent sacrococcygeal
      teratoma: A systematic review.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      A subgroup analysis of articles that measured serum AFP levels in all patients (n = 6, 136
      patients, 14 recurrences) showed a sensitivity and specificity of 79% and 95%, respectively.
    explanation: >-
      The figures from the subgroup in which everyone was measured, less exposed than the review's
      figures across all included studies to the selective reporting the review's caveat describes.
      Fourteen recurrences.
  - reference: PMID:32376010
    reference_title: >-
      Diagnostic accuracy of serum alpha-fetoprotein levels in diagnosing recurrent sacrococcygeal
      teratoma: A systematic review.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Diagnostic accuracy of serum AFP levels to detect recurrent SCT seems promising, though
      sensitivity could be overestimated since serum AFP levels are mainly described in patients
      with elevated AFP levels or at recurrent SCT.
    explanation: >-
      The authors' own caveat on the sensitivity for recurrence, behind the description's warning.
      The subgroup above, in which everyone was measured, is less exposed to that selection.
  - reference: PMID:9592840
    reference_title: >-
      Alpha 1-fetoprotein (AFP) reference values in infants up to 2 years of age.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: INDIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      In the first 4 weeks of life, AFP levels decreased by 50% in 5.1 days in term babies.
    explanation: >-
      The steepness of the normal decline in term babies, which is what makes a single infant value
      hard to read. From a study of 524 samples from infants up to two years of age, not from this
      disease.
- name: Histopathological examination of the resected specimen
  diagnosis_term:
    preferred_term: histopathological examination of the whole specimen
    term:
      id: NCIT:C18190
      label: Histopathologic Examination
  description: >-
    Mature, immature or malignant, and whether the margins are clear. What makes the histology worth
    reporting in that detail is that microscopic yolk sac foci inside an otherwise mature teratoma
    raise the recurrence rate more than tenfold. No cited source says how the specimen should be
    sampled.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:39016163
    reference_title: >-
      Impact of microscopic deposits of yolk sac tumor on recurrence of mature sacrococcygeal
      teratoma.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: BACKGROUND
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      In particular, prior studies have not investigated whether microscopic deposits of yolk sac
      tumor (YST) in otherwise mature teratomas lead to higher recurrence rates.
    explanation: >-
      The question this row exists to answer, stated as unanswered by the study that answered it.
  - reference: PMID:33906346
    reference_title: >-
      Sacrococcygeal Teratoma : A Tumor at the Center of Embryogenesis.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Incomplete resection and malignant histology are risk factors for recurrence.
    explanation: >-
      The two things this examination establishes, and why both matter.
- name: Postnatal MRI or CT
  diagnosis_term:
    preferred_term: postnatal MRI or CT
    term:
      id: NCIT:C16502
      label: Diagnostic Imaging Testing
  description: >-
    Cross-sectional imaging after birth. In one centre's series every live-born infant had MRI or CT
    after birth, and it correlated strongly with the prenatal ultrasound in every prenatally
    diagnosed case. Both tumours in that series that were malignant at diagnosis were found only
    after birth, with neither seen before it, and both were imaged after birth, mainly with MRI.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:40269769
    reference_title: >-
      Sacrococcygeal teratoma - prognosis based on prenatal ultrasound diagnosis, single-center
      experience and literature review.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      All live newborns underwent postnatal MRI or CT imaging, which strongly correlated with
      prenatal ultrasound findings in all prenatally diagnosed cases.
    explanation: >-
      Postnatal cross-sectional imaging against the prenatal scan, in one centre's live-born
      infants.
  - reference: PMID:40269769
    reference_title: >-
      Sacrococcygeal teratoma - prognosis based on prenatal ultrasound diagnosis, single-center
      experience and literature review.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      In our study group, both cases of malignant SCT (100%) were diagnosed postnatally, with none
      detected during the prenatal period.
    explanation: >-
      Both tumours of that series that were malignant at diagnosis were found after birth.
  - reference: PMID:40269769
    reference_title: >-
      Sacrococcygeal teratoma - prognosis based on prenatal ultrasound diagnosis, single-center
      experience and literature review.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Imaging techniques, primarily postnatal MRI, were performed in both cases.
    explanation: >-
      How the two malignant tumours were imaged after birth: mainly with MRI.
imaging_findings:
- name: Sacral mass on prenatal ultrasound
  modality: ULTRASOUND
  imaging_finding_term:
    preferred_term: heterogeneous solid, cystic or mixed sacral mass
  phenotype_term:
    preferred_term: sacrococcygeal mass
    term:
      id: HP:0030736
      label: Sacrococcygeal teratoma
  located_in:
    preferred_term: sacral region
    term:
      id: UBERON:0005473
      label: sacral region
  description: >-
    A heterogeneous mass arising from the sacral region, solid, cystic or mixed, with a variable
    blood supply. It is looked for on the detailed mid-pregnancy scan and is sometimes seen earlier
    or only later: in one centre's 16 cases, three were found at 13 to 16 weeks, nine at the
    second-trimester screening, two after 30 weeks and two only after birth.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:36326365
    reference_title: >-
      A single-center experience of magnetic resonance imaging findings of fetal sacrococcygeal
      teratomas.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: BACKGROUND
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      On US examination, it is seen as a mass lesion with a heterogeneous echo pattern containing
      solid and cystic structures and may show varying degrees of blood supply
    explanation: >-
      The appearance on ultrasound, as a fetal MRI series introduces it, citing earlier work.
  - reference: PMID:40269769
    reference_title: >-
      Sacrococcygeal teratoma - prognosis based on prenatal ultrasound diagnosis, single-center
      experience and literature review.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      The sacrococcygeal teratoma is mainly presented as a heterogeneous, well-defined mass arising
      from the sacrum region
    explanation: >-
      A similar description in a single-centre series' review of the literature.
  - reference: PMID:40269769
    reference_title: >-
      Sacrococcygeal teratoma - prognosis based on prenatal ultrasound diagnosis, single-center
      experience and literature review.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Three cases (18.8%) of SCT were detected by ultrasound examination early—in the 13th, 14th,
      and 16th weeks of pregnancy; nine more during the second-trimester screening (56.2%); two
      after the 30th week of gestation (12.5%); and two cases postnatally (12.5%).
    explanation: >-
      When the tumour was found in one centre's 16 cases, including in the first trimester.
  - reference: PMID:38969517
    reference_title: "Prenatal diagnosis in estimating the prognosis of sacrococcygeal teratoma."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      The diagnosis is based on ultrasound examination, especially the evaluation of the detailed
      morphology of the foetus in the 20th week of pregnancy.
    explanation: >-
      The mid-pregnancy anatomy scan as the occasion of diagnosis, in a review by largely the same
      authors.
- name: Cystic or solid tumour content
  modality: ULTRASOUND
  imaging_finding_term:
    preferred_term: cystic, mixed or solid tumour
  description: >-
    How much of the tumour is solid. In one centre's 37 fetuses every cystic tumour did well, and
    every fetus with a poor prognosis had a morphology score of 3 or more, a score the abstract does
    not define; a three-centre series, which evaluated 79 fetuses and excluded eleven terminations,
    found solid morphology a predictor of poor prognosis, but neither it nor any other factor was
    independent on multivariate analysis. On fetal MRI in another series, four of eleven tumours
    were completely cystic and seven mixed or solid.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:23845611
    reference_title: >-
      Tumor metrics and morphology predict poor prognosis in prenatally diagnosed sacrococcygeal
      teratoma: a 25-year experience at a single institution.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Patients with cystic SCT all had good prognosis.
    explanation: >-
      Every cystic tumour did well, in 37 fetuses; the abstract does not say how many were cystic.
  - reference: PMID:23845611
    reference_title: >-
      Tumor metrics and morphology predict poor prognosis in prenatally diagnosed sacrococcygeal
      teratoma: a 25-year experience at a single institution.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      All patients with poor prognosis had a morphology score ≥ 3, which is a significant predictor
      of poor prognosis (p <0.0001).
    explanation: >-
      The morphology score behind the threshold of 3 that the entry's diagnosis row mentions; the
      abstract does not define the score.
  - reference: PMID:25783370
    reference_title: >-
      Predictors of poor prognosis in prenatally diagnosed sacrococcygeal teratoma: A
      multiinstitutional review.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Solid tumor morphology and presence of hydrops were found to be predictors of poor prognosis.
    explanation: >-
      Solid morphology as a predictor of poor prognosis, in a three-centre series that evaluated 79
      fetuses and excluded eleven terminations.
  - reference: PMID:25783370
    reference_title: >-
      Predictors of poor prognosis in prenatally diagnosed sacrococcygeal teratoma: A
      multiinstitutional review.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      None of the factors associated with poor prognosis were independent predictors on multivariate
      analysis.
    explanation: >-
      The same series' caveat: no factor, morphology included, was independent on multivariate
      analysis.
  - reference: PMID:36326365
    reference_title: >-
      A single-center experience of magnetic resonance imaging findings of fetal sacrococcygeal
      teratomas.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      On MRI, sacrococcygeal teratomas (n = 11) were completely cystic in four fetuses, mixed and
      solid in seven (Table).
    explanation: >-
      How the eleven tumours of one fetal MRI series divided between cystic and mixed or solid.
- name: Hypervascular tumour on Doppler ultrasound
  modality: ULTRASOUND
  imaging_finding_term:
    preferred_term: hypervascular tumour
  description: >-
    A tumour with a rich blood supply on Doppler ultrasound. A meta-analysis lists a hypervascular
    tumour among the factors associated with cardiac failure that predict a poor outcome, and a
    fetal MRI series notes, citing earlier work, that predominantly solid and highly vascularised
    tumours do worse than mainly avascular cystic ones.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:37964422
    reference_title: >-
      Prognostic accuracy of factors associated with poor outcome in prenatally diagnosed
      sacrococcygeal teratoma: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Factors associated with cardiac failure such as cardiomegaly, hypervascular tumor, solid tumor
      morphology, fetal hydrops, placentomegaly, and TFR >0.12 were found to be predictive of poor
      outcome.
    explanation: >-
      Hypervascular tumour among the predictors of poor outcome in a meta-analysis of 11 studies.
  - reference: PMID:36326365
    reference_title: >-
      A single-center experience of magnetic resonance imaging findings of fetal sacrococcygeal
      teratomas.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: BACKGROUND
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Predominantly solid and highly vascularized masses demonstrate a worse prognosis than tumors
      that are mainly avascular and cystic in appearance
    explanation: >-
      The contrast between solid, highly vascularised tumours and avascular cystic ones, stated as
      background with a citation.
  - reference: PMID:40269769
    reference_title: >-
      Sacrococcygeal teratoma - prognosis based on prenatal ultrasound diagnosis, single-center
      experience and literature review.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: INDIRECT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      ultrasound examinations focusing on tumor characteristics, including tumor size, the
      predominance of solid or cystic components, vascularization assessed by Doppler flow
    explanation: >-
      Doppler as the way the tumour's blood supply is assessed, from one centre's methods. Indirect:
      it names the assessment, not a finding.
- name: Solid tumour volume index on fetal MRI
  modality: MRI
  imaging_finding_term:
    preferred_term: solid tumour volume index
  description: >-
    The solid part of the tumour's volume, measured on fetal MRI and divided by estimated fetal
    weight. Above 0.09, fetuses were 120 times more likely to develop the high-output state or
    hydrops, with a sensitivity of 81.25% and a specificity of 100%; total tumour volume over fetal
    weight above 0.16 did less well. From 31 fetuses in one retrospective chart review.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:23773720
    reference_title: >-
      Prenatal solid tumor volume index: novel prenatal predictor of adverse outcome in
      sacrococcygeal teratoma.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Total tumor volume and percent of solid component were calculated by magnetic resonance
      imaging and then normalized by dividing them by either head circumference or EFW.
    explanation: >-
      How the index is made: volumes from MRI, divided by head circumference or estimated fetal
      weight.
  - reference: PMID:23773720
    reference_title: >-
      Prenatal solid tumor volume index: novel prenatal predictor of adverse outcome in
      sacrococcygeal teratoma.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      At a STVI >0.09, the patient was 120 times more likely to develop HCOS/hydrops (P < 0.0001)
      with 81.25% sensitivity and 100% specificity.
    explanation: >-
      The index's threshold and accuracy, in 31 fetuses.
  - reference: PMID:23773720
    reference_title: >-
      Prenatal solid tumor volume index: novel prenatal predictor of adverse outcome in
      sacrococcygeal teratoma.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      At a total tumor volume/EFW >0.16, the patient was 17 times more likely to develop
      HCOS/hydrops (P = 0.001) with 81.25% sensitivity and 86.67% specificity.
    explanation: >-
      The total-volume version of the same ratio, with lower specificity.
  - reference: PMID:23773720
    reference_title: >-
      Prenatal solid tumor volume index: novel prenatal predictor of adverse outcome in
      sacrococcygeal teratoma.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      While total tumor volume aids in stratifying patients into high risk categories, STVI (solid
      tumor volume/EFW) is a better predictor of adverse outcomes.
    explanation: >-
      The authors' comparison of the two.
- name: Solid tumour volume to head volume ratio
  modality: ULTRASOUND
  imaging_finding_term:
    preferred_term: solid tumour volume to head volume ratio
  description: >-
    The solid tumour volume divided by the head volume, both from ultrasound. In one series of 28
    fetuses no fetus with a ratio below 1 died, while 11 of 18 with a ratio above 1 did; 97.3% of
    sonograms with a ratio above 1 showed one or more abnormal signs, against 20% below it.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:19752518
    reference_title: "Prognostic role of tumor-head volume ratio in fetal sacrococcygeal teratoma."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Head volume (HV) and total tumor volume were calculated from sonograms. Amount of cystic tumor
      was estimated to determine solid tumor volume (STV) for the STV/HV ratio.
    explanation: >-
      How the ratio is made, from sonograms.
  - reference: PMID:19752518
    reference_title: "Prognostic role of tumor-head volume ratio in fetal sacrococcygeal teratoma."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      There was no mortality in fetuses with a ratio of <1, while 11/18 (61%) of fetuses with ratio
      >1 died (p = 0.003).
    explanation: >-
      Death by ratio: none below 1, and 11 of 18 above it.
  - reference: PMID:19752518
    reference_title: "Prognostic role of tumor-head volume ratio in fetal sacrococcygeal teratoma."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Twenty percent of sonograms with STV/HV <1 and 97.3% with STV/HV >1 were associated with 1 or
      more abnormal sonographic signs (p = 0.000).
    explanation: >-
      Abnormal signs by ratio, counted per sonogram rather than per fetus.
- name: Tumour volume over biparietal diameter
  modality: ULTRASOUND
  imaging_finding_term:
    preferred_term: tumour volume index
  description: >-
    Tumour volume divided by the biparietal diameter, to adjust for gestational age. Above 60 cm3
    per cm it identified every neonatal death in a series of 25 children, six of whom died; the same
    sentence reports two cord-blood markers, which are not imaging findings.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:29399854
    reference_title: "Antenatal Prediction of Neonatal Survival in Sacrococcygeal Teratoma."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      To adjust the gestational age, the tumor volume index (tumor volume/biparietal diameter) was
      adopted in the analysis.
    explanation: >-
      How the index is made.
  - reference: PMID:29399854
    reference_title: "Antenatal Prediction of Neonatal Survival in Sacrococcygeal Teratoma."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      A tumor volume index of greater than 60 cm3 /cm, elevated NT-pro-BNP (>2000 pg/mL), and
      elevated cTnT (>0.08 ng/mL) had sensitivity of 100% for prediction of neonatal death.
    explanation: >-
      The threshold for neonatal death. Only the volume index is claimed here; the two cord-blood
      markers in the same sentence are not imaging.
  - reference: PMID:29399854
    reference_title: "Antenatal Prediction of Neonatal Survival in Sacrococcygeal Teratoma."
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      The rate of neonatal death was 24% (6 of 25).
    explanation: >-
      The denominator behind the 100% sensitivity: six deaths among 25.
- name: Tumour growth on serial ultrasound
  modality: ULTRASOUND
  imaging_finding_term:
    preferred_term: tumour growth rate
  description: >-
    How fast the tumour grows between scans. In five centres' 55 fetuses, growth velocity in
    millimetres per week was the only independent factor associated with a poor perinatal outcome;
    in a French multicentre series of 28, only the volume growth rate stayed significant after
    adjustment, and a volume growth rate above 18.01 cm3 per week and a volume above 245 cm3 went
    with a poor outcome. The two series define a poor outcome differently.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:39482803
    reference_title: >-
      Growth velocity of fetal sacrococcygeal teratoma as predictor of perinatal morbidity and
      mortality: multicenter study.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      On stepwise logistic regression analysis, tumor growth velocity was the only remaining
      independent factor associated with poor perinatal outcome (odds ratio (OR) (per 1-mm/week
      increase), 1.48 (95% CI, 1.22-1.97), P = 0.001).
    explanation: >-
      Growth velocity as the only independent factor, in 55 fetuses from five centres.
  - reference: PMID:39482803
    reference_title: >-
      Growth velocity of fetal sacrococcygeal teratoma as predictor of perinatal morbidity and
      mortality: multicenter study.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      The primary outcome was the occurrence of poor perinatal outcome, defined as prenatal death
      (including termination), or neonatal death or severe compromise (hemorrhagic shock).
    explanation: >-
      That series' poor outcome: death, including termination, or severe neonatal compromise.
  - reference: PMID:40261238
    reference_title: >-
      Prognostic Value of Antenatal Tumor Growth Rate Parameters in Fetal Sacrococcygeal Teratoma: A
      French Multicenter Retrospective Study.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      After adjusting by multivariate analysis, only a higher tumor volume growth rate (p = 0.043)
      was significantly associated with extended perinatal morbidity and mortality.
    explanation: >-
      In a second series of 28, only the volume growth rate survived adjustment.
  - reference: PMID:40261238
    reference_title: >-
      Prognostic Value of Antenatal Tumor Growth Rate Parameters in Fetal Sacrococcygeal Teratoma: A
      French Multicenter Retrospective Study.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      A tumor volume growth rate > 18.01 cm3/week and a volume > 245 cm3 at any stage of pregnancy
      were associated with a poor perinatal outcome.
    explanation: >-
      That series' thresholds.
  - reference: PMID:40261238
    reference_title: >-
      Prognostic Value of Antenatal Tumor Growth Rate Parameters in Fetal Sacrococcygeal Teratoma: A
      French Multicenter Retrospective Study.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Among the 28 cases, fetuses that died or required transfusion/vasopressors at birth presented
      with a higher growth rate for all three parameters.
    explanation: >-
      That series' poor outcome includes transfusion or vasopressors at birth, a different
      definition.
- name: Signs of a high-output heart on fetal echocardiography
  modality: ULTRASOUND
  phenotype_term:
    preferred_term: cardiomegaly
    term:
      id: HP:0001640
      label: Cardiomegaly
  description: >-
    Abnormal size and systolic function of the fetal heart, including a raised combined ventricular
    output. In a series of 19 fetuses with this tumour or a twin reversed arterial perfusion
    sequence, every fetus that later died or developed hydrops had at least one of a cardiothoracic
    ratio above 0.5, a combined ventricular output above 550 ml/min/kg, tricuspid or mitral
    regurgitation, or a mitral valve Z-score above 2, and none of those who did well had any;
    diastolic function did not separate them. The 550 is that mixed cohort's cut-off for an abnormal
    output, and the entry's high-output node uses another series' definition of 625.
  notes: >-
    HP:0001640 Cardiomegaly anchors the row's size sign, a cardiothoracic ratio above 0.5. The other
    three signs, a combined ventricular output above 550 ml/min/kg, tricuspid or mitral
    regurgitation and a mitral valve Z-score above 2, are output and valve findings that the term
    does not cover.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:22086180
    reference_title: >-
      Echocardiographic risk stratification of fetuses with sacrococcygeal teratoma and
      twin-reversed arterial perfusion.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: INDIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      At least one of the following was present in each group A fetus: CTR >0.5, CVO >550 ml/min/kg,
      tricuspid or mitral regurgitation, or mitral valve Z-score >2. No group B fetus had any of
      these abnormalities.
    explanation: >-
      The four signs, at least one of which was present in every fetus that did badly. Indirect: the
      cohort mixes 11 fetuses with this tumour and 8 with the twin sequence, and the abstract does
      not split them.
  - reference: PMID:22086180
    reference_title: >-
      Echocardiographic risk stratification of fetuses with sacrococcygeal teratoma and
      twin-reversed arterial perfusion.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: INDIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Fetal echocardiography can identify abnormalities of cardiac size and systolic, but not
      diastolic, function in all fetuses who subsequently died or developed hydrops.
    explanation: >-
      The authors' conclusion, from the same mixed cohort.
  - reference: PMID:22086180
    reference_title: >-
      Echocardiographic risk stratification of fetuses with sacrococcygeal teratoma and
      twin-reversed arterial perfusion.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: INDIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Group A had worse CVPS (8.5 vs. 10, p < 0.01) and higher CTR (0.37 vs. 0.30, p = 0.04).
    explanation: >-
      Worse cardiovascular profile score and larger heart in the poor-outcome group.
- name: Raised fetal middle cerebral artery peak systolic velocity
  modality: ULTRASOUND
  imaging_finding_term:
    preferred_term: elevated fetal middle cerebral artery peak systolic velocity
    term:
      id: HP:0034191
      label: Elevated fetal middle cerebral artery peak systolic velocity
  phenotype_term:
    preferred_term: elevated fetal middle cerebral artery peak systolic velocity
    term:
      id: HP:0034191
      label: Elevated fetal middle cerebral artery peak systolic velocity
  description: >-
    A middle cerebral artery peak systolic velocity of 1.5 multiples of the median or more, the
    Doppler sign used for fetal anaemia. In one centre's 36 fetuses with this tumour, 14 had it, and
    it went with more neonatal deaths, a higher risk of perinatal death and earlier delivery; the
    authors say the finding needs validation before it guides management.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:42815687
    reference_title: >-
      Clinical outcomes associated with abnormal middle cerebral artery Doppler velocities in fetal
      sacrococcygeal teratoma.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Cases were stratified by fetal middle cerebral artery (MCA) Doppler status (normal vs
      abnormal), with abnormal defined as a peak systolic velocity ≥1.5 multiples of the median
      (MoM).
    explanation: >-
      The study's definition of an abnormal velocity.
  - reference: PMID:42815687
    reference_title: >-
      Clinical outcomes associated with abnormal middle cerebral artery Doppler velocities in fetal
      sacrococcygeal teratoma.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Among 36 fetuses with prenatally diagnosed SCT, 14 (39%) had abnormal MCA Doppler velocities.
    explanation: >-
      How often it was found, in one tertiary centre.
  - reference: PMID:42815687
    reference_title: >-
      Clinical outcomes associated with abnormal middle cerebral artery Doppler velocities in fetal
      sacrococcygeal teratoma.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Abnormal MCA Dopplers were also associated with higher neonatal mortality (40% vs 0%, P<.01),
      and, in the full cohort, with increased odds of perinatal death (OR 13.3, 95% CI 2.55-106),
      5-minute Apgar <7 (50% vs 10%, P=.03), and earlier gestational age at delivery (28 vs 36
      weeks, P<.01).
    explanation: >-
      Its associations with death, Apgar score and gestation at delivery; the confidence interval of
      the odds ratio runs from 2.55 to 106.
  - reference: PMID:42815687
    reference_title: >-
      Clinical outcomes associated with abnormal middle cerebral artery Doppler velocities in fetal
      sacrococcygeal teratoma.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      These findings suggest that MCA Doppler assessment may help identify higher-risk cases but
      require validation in larger, multicenter cohorts before informing clinical management.
    explanation: >-
      The authors' caveat.
  - reference: PMID:42815687
    reference_title: >-
      Clinical outcomes associated with abnormal middle cerebral artery Doppler velocities in fetal
      sacrococcygeal teratoma.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: BACKGROUND
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Although middle cerebral artery peak systolic velocity is widely used to assess fetal anemia,
      its prognostic value in pregnancies complicated by sacrococcygeal teratoma is not well
      established.
    explanation: >-
      Why the velocity is measured at all, as the abstract's background states it.
- name: Extent within the pelvis and spinal canal on fetal MRI
  modality: MRI
  imaging_finding_term:
    preferred_term: intrapelvic or intraspinal tumour extension
  description: >-
    How far the tumour reaches into the pelvis, the abdomen and the spinal canal. In eleven fetuses
    imaged with ultrasound and then MRI, the two agreed overall, but MRI was better for intrapelvic
    and abdominal extension, a displaced colon and urinary tract complications, and in one fetus
    showed an extension into the spinal canal that ultrasound missed. About 2% of these tumours
    extend into the spinal canal, a figure a second single-centre series cites from earlier work.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:36326365
    reference_title: >-
      A single-center experience of magnetic resonance imaging findings of fetal sacrococcygeal
      teratomas.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      US findings are found strongly correlated with MRI findings.
    explanation: >-
      Overall agreement between ultrasound and MRI, in eleven fetuses.
  - reference: PMID:36326365
    reference_title: >-
      A single-center experience of magnetic resonance imaging findings of fetal sacrococcygeal
      teratomas.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      MRI was superior to US for detecting displacement of the colon (n = 3),
      intrapelvic-intraabdominal extension (n = 1), urinary tract complication (n = 2), and
      intraspinal extension (n = 1).
    explanation: >-
      What MRI showed better, with the number of fetuses for each.
  - reference: PMID:36326365
    reference_title: >-
      A single-center experience of magnetic resonance imaging findings of fetal sacrococcygeal
      teratomas.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      An agreement on the extent of each mass was observed in eight patients, disagreement in one
      fetus was an extension of the tumor within the spinal canal recognized only at MR and
      assessment of intrapelvic-abdominal extension was superior in MRI.
    explanation: >-
      The one fetus whose spinal extension only MRI showed.
  - reference: PMID:40269769
    reference_title: >-
      Sacrococcygeal teratoma - prognosis based on prenatal ultrasound diagnosis, single-center
      experience and literature review.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: BACKGROUND
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      About 2% of sacrococcygeal teratomas extend into the spinal canal
    explanation: >-
      How often the tumour reaches the spinal canal, stated as background with a citation.
- name: Bladder displacement and hydronephrosis on prenatal imaging
  modality: MRI
  phenotype_term:
    preferred_term: hydronephrosis
    term:
      id: HP:0000126
      label: Hydronephrosis
  description: >-
    Signs that the pelvic part of the tumour presses on the urinary tract. In eleven fetuses, MRI
    showed a displaced bladder in three and hydronephrosis in three, while ultrasound showed only
    the hydronephrosis; a single-centre review lists obstruction of the pelvic organs among the
    ultrasound markers of a poor long-term outcome.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:36326365
    reference_title: >-
      A single-center experience of magnetic resonance imaging findings of fetal sacrococcygeal
      teratomas.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      The bladder displacement was observed in 3 of 11 fetuses (27.2%), and bilateral hydronephrosis
      in 2 fetus and unilateral hydronephrosis in 1 fetus on MRI, but only hydronephrosis was
      detected by sonography.
    explanation: >-
      Bladder displacement and hydronephrosis on MRI against ultrasound, in eleven fetuses.
  - reference: PMID:40269769
    reference_title: >-
      Sacrococcygeal teratoma - prognosis based on prenatal ultrasound diagnosis, single-center
      experience and literature review.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Other ultrasound markers predicting poor long-term prognosis are associated with complications
      due to intrapelvic organ obstruction - hydronephrosis with ureter dilatation, mega vesica,
      hydronephrosis, or polyhydramnios.
    explanation: >-
      Obstruction signs among markers of a poor long-term outcome, in the review section of a
      single-centre series.
- name: Recurrent mature teratoma on surveillance MRI
  modality: MRI
  imaging_finding_term:
    preferred_term: recurrent mature teratoma
  description: >-
    A recurrence of mature teratoma found on MRI in follow-up after resection. In one series the two
    mature recurrences were found on surveillance MRI, while all five malignant recurrences were
    found by a rising alpha-fetoprotein.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:39016163
    reference_title: >-
      Impact of microscopic deposits of yolk sac tumor on recurrence of mature sacrococcygeal
      teratoma.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Five patients demonstrated malignant recurrence and were all detected by a rising
      alpha-fetoprotein (AFP), while two patients demonstrated recurrence of mature teratoma and
      were detected on surveillance magnetic resonance imaging (MRI).
    explanation: >-
      Mature recurrences found on surveillance MRI, while the malignant ones were found by
      alpha-fetoprotein.
treatments:
- name: Complete resection with the coccyx
  therapeutic_modality: SURGERY
  treatment_term:
    preferred_term: tumour resection
    term:
      id: NCIT:C164212
      label: Tumor Resection
  description: >-
    The definitive treatment, done after birth in most patients. Completeness is what matters:
    positive margins raise the recurrence rate about tenfold in one series, and incomplete resection
    is named as a risk factor for recurrence by a review. The coccyx is removed with the tumour: two
    series report doing so in their own patients, and a review names failure to remove it among the
    primary drivers of recurrence.
  notes: >-
    The row's name includes the coccyx because each cited source that mentions the coccyx describes
    removing it with the tumour.
  target_mechanisms:
  - target: Tridermal Teratomatous Mass at the Sacrococcyx
    treatment_effect: BYPASSES
    description: >-
      Resection removes the mass. It acts on nothing above it - the misplaced germ cell and whatever
      reprogrammed it are not addressed - which is the reason a complete resection is followed for
      years rather than discharged.
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:39016163
      reference_title: >-
        Impact of microscopic deposits of yolk sac tumor on recurrence of mature sacrococcygeal
        teratoma.
      supports: SUPPORT
      directness: INDIRECT
      quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
      evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
      snippet: >-
        Recurrence was more likely in patients with microscopic YST [5/9 (56%) vs. 2/47 (4%), p =
        0.021] and positive margins [6/24 (35%) vs. 1/32 (3.1%), p = 0.030].
      explanation: >-
        The margin result: 35% recurrence against 3.1%. INDIRECT for this link because recurrence
        is a disease outcome rather than a measurement on the mass, and the arms were not
        randomised.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:25746708
    reference_title: >-
      Malignant transformation in sacrococcygeal teratoma and in presacral teratoma associated with
      Currarino syndrome: a comparative study.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      In SCT, malignancy and recurrence risk are high.
    explanation: >-
      The authors' stated reason for the next sentence, which is this row's recommendation.
  - reference: PMID:25746708
    reference_title: >-
      Malignant transformation in sacrococcygeal teratoma and in presacral teratoma associated with
      Currarino syndrome: a comparative study.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Therefore, early and complete resection is mandatory.
    explanation: >-
      The recommendation, from a national comparative analysis of 205 sacrococcygeal and 16
      Currarino patients. It is a recommendation, not a comparison against delayed or partial
      resection.
  - reference: PMID:36326365
    reference_title: >-
      A single-center experience of magnetic resonance imaging findings of fetal sacrococcygeal
      teratomas.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: BACKGROUND
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Treatment is with surgical excision inclusive of coccygectomy with additional chemotherapy for
