      malignant ones.
    explanation: >-
      Excision with the coccyx as the treatment, stated in a fetal MRI series' discussion.
  - reference: PMID:40269769
    reference_title: >-
      Sacrococcygeal teratoma - prognosis based on prenatal ultrasound diagnosis, single-center
      experience and literature review.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Coccyx removal is indicated as part of the surgical treatment, which prevents local recurrence
    explanation: >-
      Coccyx removal as part of the operation, which a single-centre series with a literature review
      says prevents local recurrence, citing earlier work.
  - reference: PMID:40269769
    reference_title: >-
      Sacrococcygeal teratoma - prognosis based on prenatal ultrasound diagnosis, single-center
      experience and literature review.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      This approach was applied to all operated newborns in our group.
    explanation: >-
      The same series' own practice: the approach of the sentence before, coccyx removal, in every
      newborn it operated on.
  - reference: PMID:42219219
    reference_title: >-
      Antenatal and Postnatal Management of Sacrococcygeal Teratoma.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Surgical management relies on multidisciplinary perinatal planning and includes complete
      oncologic resection with coccygectomy.
    explanation: >-
      Complete resection with coccygectomy as the surgical management, in a review.
  - reference: PMID:42219219

- name: Fetal radiofrequency ablation of the feeding vessels
  therapeutic_modality: SURGERY
  treatment_term:
    preferred_term: radiofrequency ablation
    term:
      id: NCIT:C15666
      label: Radiofrequency Ablation
  description: >-
    Interrupting the tumour's blood supply before birth, to reverse the high-output state rather
    than to remove the tumour. The first report of it is also the clearest statement of its limit:
    ablating most of the tumour mass was unnecessary and killed two of four fetuses. In a 2024
    systematic review survival was 45.8% (22 of 48) after percutaneous procedures as a group and 12
    of 18 (67%) after radiofrequency ablation itself, against 71.0% (66 of 93) without
    intervention; in a 2011 cohort it was 6 of 8 after fetal intervention (radiofrequency ablation
    in six, shunting alone in two) against 14 of 14 without, an outcome the authors call similar
    despite the treated fetuses' worse prognostic features. The groups are not alike: in the review
    fetal intervention is indicated for fetuses with hydrops or cardiac dysfunction, and hydrops
    and cardiac failure were rarer without it; in the 2011 cohort the treated fetuses' tumours were
    larger, rapidly growing and more often vascular, with associated polyhydramnios or
    cardiomegaly. The review says it could not evaluate the effectiveness of fetal surgery of any
    type against no fetal intervention.
  notes: >-
    The review's case table lists 18 radiofrequency ablations; four are from the first report
    (2001), six from the 2011 cohort and two from the 2014 case series, all three cited on this row,
    so the review's 12 of 18 is not independent of them. The review's abstract and results text give
    p = 0.568 for survival after open surgery against percutaneous intervention, and its Table 1
    gives 0.645 for the same comparison; the sentence quoted on this row with p = 0.568 is the
    abstract's.
  target_mechanisms:
  - target: High-Output Cardiac State from Tumour Vascular Steal
    treatment_effect: INHIBITS
    description: >-
      The target is the shunt, not the tumour. Reducing flow through the feeding vessels is enough to
      reverse the failure; the tumour is resected after birth.
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:11228510
      reference_title: >-
        Radiofrequency ablation of human fetal sacrococcygeal teratoma.
      supports: SUPPORT
      directness: INDIRECT
      quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
      evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
      snippet: >-
        Targeted ablation of the feeding tumor vessels diminishes blood flow sufficiently to
        reverse high-output fetal heart failure.
      explanation: >-
        The mechanism of the treatment stated exactly as this link claims it. Four fetuses, so it
        is the authors' conclusion from a first report rather than a measured effect size.

- name: Open fetal resection
  therapeutic_modality: SURGERY
  treatment_term:
    preferred_term: open fetal resection of the tumour
    term:
      id: NCIT:C164212
      label: Tumor Resection
  description: >-
    Resection of the tumour in utero for a fetus in progressive high-output failure. The field has
    moved away from it towards the minimally invasive techniques above, and the cited survival
    figures do not separate the two by much. Survival after open surgery was 56.2% (9 of 16) in a
    2024 systematic review, against 71.0% (66 of 93) without intervention. The review reports
    survival as significantly higher without intervention than in the cohorts treated by fetal
    surgery, without a p-value for that comparison and without saying whether it holds for open
    surgery alone, but says it did not aim to compare the two, because fetal intervention is
    indicated for the severe forms with hydrops or cardiac dysfunction, and that it could not
    evaluate the effectiveness of fetal surgery of any type against no fetal intervention.
  notes: >-
    Bound to Tumor Resection (NCIT:C164212), as the complete-resection and pre-emptive delivery rows
    are: the row's link to the high-output state runs through removing the tumour. NCIT defines the
    term as the removal of cancerous tissue; the three rows use it for the removal of a tumour that
    may be benign. Label searches of the local NCIT build for l~fetal surgery, l~fetal surgical,
    l~intrauterine surgery and l~fetal resection return nothing. The review's abstract and results
    text give p = 0.568 for survival after open surgery against percutaneous intervention, and its
    Table 1 gives 0.645 for the same comparison; the sentence quoted on this row with p = 0.568 is
    the abstract's.
  target_mechanisms:
  - target: High-Output Cardiac State from Tumour Vascular Steal
    treatment_effect: INHIBITS
    description: >-
      Removing the tumour before birth removes the shunt. The cost is maternal morbidity and preterm
      delivery, which is why the alternative above exists.

- name: Amnioreduction
  therapeutic_modality: SURGERY
  treatment_term:
    preferred_term: amnioreduction
    term:
      id: NCIT:C15310
      label: Paracentesis
  description: >-
    Needle drainage of excess amniotic fluid. It treats a consequence of the tumour, not the tumour:
    a 2024 systematic review of fetal surgery left it out because its intention is not to reduce
    tumour size. In a 2004 series the indications given for cyst aspiration and amnioreduction
    together were maternal discomfort, preterm labour and prevention of tumour rupture at delivery,
    and the series' authors call amnioreduction, cyst aspiration and surgical debulking potentially
    life-saving.
  notes: >-
    No NCIT label names amnioreduction: a label search of the local NCIT build for l~amnioreduction
    returns nothing. Paracentesis (NCIT:C15310), which NCIT defines as the removal of excess fluid
    via needle puncture from any body cavity, is bound; NCIT files Amniocentesis (NCIT:C52009) under
    it. Apart from laboratory tests on amniotic fluid, the only procedures that l~amnio returns are
    Amniocentesis, which NCIT defines as a diagnostic procedure, and Amnioinfusion (NCIT:C92729),
    which instils fluid.
  target_mechanisms:
  - target: Polyhydramnios
    treatment_effect: INHIBITS
    description: >-
      Removes the excess amniotic fluid that the high-output state helps produce.

- name: Pre-emptive early delivery and immediate resection
  therapeutic_modality: SURGERY
  treatment_term:
    preferred_term: pre-emptive early delivery with immediate postnatal resection
    term:
      id: NCIT:C164212
      label: Tumor Resection
  description: >-
    Delivering early, between 27 and 32 weeks, in response to impending fetal or maternal
    decompensation, and resecting the tumour straight after birth, instead of fetal surgery or
    waiting. In one centre's series 9 of 11 fetuses delivered this way survived and none died of
    prematurity; the authors, reporting favourable outcomes in the absence of hydrops before 27
    weeks or tumour rupture in utero, say their single-centre experience supports pre-emptive
    delivery for selected cases.
  notes: >-
    Bound to Tumor Resection (NCIT:C164212), as the complete-resection and open fetal resection rows
    are. NCIT defines the term as the removal of cancerous tissue; the three rows use it for the
    removal of a tumour that may be benign. The treatment term takes one term, and the row's link to
    the high-output state runs through the resection after birth; Obstetric Procedure (NCIT:C89340)
    or Delivery Procedure (NCIT:C81179) would name only the delivery, which the row's name and
    preferred term carry instead. No more specific delivery term was available in any case: the
    series' abstract (PMID:29734172) does not give the mode of delivery, so neither Cesarean Section
    (NCIT:C46088) nor Induction of Labor (NCIT:C92814) can be chosen, and a label search of the
    local NCIT build for l~preterm delivery returns only GAIA case-definition terms.
  target_mechanisms:
  - target: High-Output Cardiac State from Tumour Vascular Steal
    treatment_effect: INHIBITS
    description: >-
      Ends the shunt by removing the tumour after birth, without operating on the fetus. The case
      report that restates the series names the absence of high-output cardiovascular failure, of
      tumour bleeding and of fetal anaemia among the conditions for its success.
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:29734172
      reference_title: >-
        Preemptive Delivery and Immediate Resection for Fetuses with High-Risk Sacrococcygeal
        Teratomas.
      supports: SUPPORT
      directness: INDIRECT
      evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
      snippet: >-
        Here we report our experience applying "preemptive" delivery to fetuses who manifest signs
        of decompensation between 27 and 32 weeks.
      explanation: >-
        The indication: signs of decompensation between 27 and 32 weeks; this row's results sentence
        adds impending maternal decompensation. INDIRECT for the link, which follows from immediate
        resection.
    - reference: PMID:30949371
      reference_title: >-
        Significant Clinical Manifestations in Ballantyne Syndrome, after a Case Report and
        Literature Review: Recognizing Preeclampsia as a Differential Diagnosis.
      supports: SUPPORT
      directness: INDIRECT
      quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
      evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
      snippet: >-
        Beyond 27 weeks' gestation, however, the risk for the development of complications related
        to the surgery increases significantly; therefore early delivery (27 to 32 weeks' gestation)
        with immediate SCT resection has been shown to be a better option than "watchful waiting"
        documented by Baumgartner et al. with a survival rate of 81.8%
      explanation: >-
        A case report's literature review, restating the 2019 single-centre series and its 81.8%
        survival: after 27 weeks the risk of complications related to fetal surgery increases, and
        early delivery with immediate resection is called a better option than watchful waiting. The
        series' abstract reports no comparison with another approach.
    - reference: PMID:30949371
      reference_title: >-
        Significant Clinical Manifestations in Ballantyne Syndrome, after a Case Report and
        Literature Review: Recognizing Preeclampsia as a Differential Diagnosis.
      supports: SUPPORT
      directness: INDIRECT
      quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
      evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
      snippet: >-
        Important considerations for the success of earlier delivery include a low compromised

      Preemptive Delivery and Immediate Resection for Fetuses with High-Risk Sacrococcygeal
      Teratomas.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Our single-center experience supports a management algorithm change to incorporate
      "preemptive" delivery for selected cases.
    explanation: >-
      The authors' recommendation, from their own series.
- name: Caesarean section for a large or vascular tumour
  therapeutic_modality: SURGERY
  treatment_term:
    preferred_term: caesarean section
    term:
      id: NCIT:C46088
      label: Cesarean Section
  description: >-
    When the tumour is large (more than 5 to 10 cm across) or highly vascular, vaginal birth is not
    recommended because of a higher risk of rupture and bleeding. The mode of delivery is chosen
    case by case; in a 2025 single-centre series 8 of the 9 delivered fetuses, two of them not
    detected before birth, were born by caesarean section, and the ninth by a spontaneous
    precipitous vaginal delivery. A tumour that is large for the fetus's weight also predicts a
    higher-risk maternal operation: a 2019 single-centre study counted open fetal surgery, classical
    caesarean delivery and EXIT as such operations, and a tumour volume to fetal weight ratio above
    0.12 at or before 24 weeks predicted one.
  target_mechanisms:
  - target: Haemorrhage into the Tumour
    treatment_effect: INHIBITS
    description: >-
      Avoids the rupture and bleeding that a vaginal birth risks with a large or highly vascular
      tumour; haemorrhage into the tumour is the nearest node the entry has for bleeding at birth.
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:40269769
      reference_title: >-
        Sacrococcygeal teratoma - prognosis based on prenatal ultrasound diagnosis, single-center
        experience and literature review.
      supports: SUPPORT
      directness: INDIRECT
      quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
      evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
      snippet: >-
        For more extensive findings (> 5-10 cm in diameter) and highly vascularized tumors, vaginal
        birth is not recommended due to a higher risk of complications (rupture, bleeding)
      explanation: >-
        The reason for caesarean section: a large or highly vascular tumour risks rupture and
        bleeding in a vaginal birth. INDIRECT: the sentence advises against vaginal birth and states
        no effect of caesarean section on the node.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:40269769
    reference_title: >-
      Sacrococcygeal teratoma - prognosis based on prenatal ultrasound diagnosis, single-center
      experience and literature review.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      The mode of delivery is selected individually.
    explanation: >-
      The choice is made case by case.
  - reference: PMID:40269769
    reference_title: >-
      Sacrococcygeal teratoma - prognosis based on prenatal ultrasound diagnosis, single-center
      experience and literature review.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Among the nine delivered fetuses (including two cases not detected prenatally), eight patients
      (88.9%) underwent cesarean section, while one case (11.1%) resulted in spontaneous precipitous
      vaginal delivery.
    explanation: >-
      Caesarean section for 8 of 9 delivered fetuses at one centre, two of them not detected before
      birth; the ninth was a spontaneous precipitous vaginal delivery.
  - reference: PMID:29495013
    reference_title: >-
      High Tumor Volume to Fetal Weight Ratio Is Associated with Worse Fetal Outcomes and Increased
      Maternal Risk in Fetuses with Sacrococcygeal Teratoma.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Increased maternal operative risk included cases necessitating open fetal surgery, classical
      cesarean delivery, or ex utero intrapartum treatment (EXIT).
    explanation: >-
      The study's definition of increased maternal operative risk, which counts classical caesarean
      delivery among the higher-risk operations: in this study a classical caesarean is a risk to
      the mother, not a reason to choose caesarean.
  - reference: PMID:29495013
    reference_title: >-
      High Tumor Volume to Fetal Weight Ratio Is Associated with Worse Fetal Outcomes and Increased
      Maternal Risk in Fetuses with Sacrococcygeal Teratoma.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      ROC analysis revealed that at <=24 weeks, TFR > 0.095 was predictive of poor fetal outcome and
      TFR > 0.12 was predictive of increased maternal operative risk.
    explanation: >-
      The finding: a tumour volume to fetal weight ratio above 0.12 at or before 24 weeks predicted
      an increased maternal operative risk, which in this study includes classical caesarean
      delivery among other operations; that outcome is a risk to the mother, not a benefit of
      caesarean.
- name: JEB chemotherapy for malignant disease
  therapeutic_modality: SMALL_MOLECULE
  treatment_term:
    preferred_term: chemotherapy
    term:
      id: NCIT:C15632
      label: Chemotherapy
    therapeutic_agent:
    - preferred_term: carboplatin
      term:
        id: CHEBI:31355
        label: carboplatin
    - preferred_term: etoposide
      term:
        id: CHEBI:4911
        label: etoposide
    - preferred_term: bleomycin
      term:
        id: CHEBI:22907
        label: bleomycin
  description: >-
    Carboplatin, etoposide and bleomycin, for malignant germ cell tumour. The regimen was developed
    across germ cell tumour sites and four of its 21 patients had sacrococcygeal primaries, so this
    row records a regimen used in this disease rather than one tested in it.
  target_mechanisms:
  - target: Malignant Yolk Sac Component
    treatment_effect: INHIBITS
    description: >-
      The malignant component is what the regimen is for; a mature teratoma does not respond to
      chemotherapy and is treated by resection alone.
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:1696831
      reference_title: >-
        'JEB'--a carboplatin based regimen for malignant germ cell tumours in children.
      supports: SUPPORT
      directness: INDIRECT
      quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
      evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
      snippet: >-
        Complete marker response was achieved in 19 out of 19 evaluable patients and complete
        remission of measurable tumour in 16 out of 19, 12 with chemotherapy alone and 4 with the
        addition of surgery.
      explanation: >-
        The response, with the marker response separated from the tumour response. INDIRECT for
        this link: the cohort is malignant germ cell tumour across sites, of which four were
        sacrococcygeal.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:1696831
    reference_title: >-
      'JEB'--a carboplatin based regimen for malignant germ cell tumours in children.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Primary sites were: testis (6), ovary (8), sacrococcyx (4), pineal gland (2) and vagina (1).
    explanation: >-
      The site breakdown, which is why this row says the regimen was used in this disease rather
      than tested in it: four of 21 patients.
  - reference: PMID:1696831
    reference_title: >-
      'JEB'--a carboplatin based regimen for malignant germ cell tumours in children.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: INDIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      It appears to have comparable efficacy to cisplatin-based regimens but with much less
      nephrotoxicity and ototoxicity and avoids the use of alkylating agents and anthracyclines.
    explanation: >-
      Why this regimen rather than a cisplatin one, in the authors' words and with their hedge:
      appears to have comparable efficacy. No randomised comparison is cited.
progression:
- phase: Prenatal
  notes: >-
    Detected before birth in 55% of pregnancies in a Finnish national register, and in 74% and 50%
    of cases in two other population-based series (only the Finnish abstract says what its share is
    counted over; see the prenatal detection row). In three hospital series of fetuses diagnosed
    before birth, the median week of diagnosis differs widely: 22 weeks in 55 fetuses, 23 in seven,
    and 30.9 in eleven. The high-output state is the route to a poor outcome that the prenatal
    predictors track, though a single-centre series of early delivery also reports a death from
    tumour rupture in the womb and one from pulmonary hypoplasia; fetuses that do well are delivered
    and operated on. Mortality including terminations is about a third in referral series and is
    driven by the terminations.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:34327722
    reference_title: >-
      Factors associated with poor outcome in fetuses prenatally diagnosed with sacrococcygeal
      teratoma.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Overall mortality was 32.1%, with a mortality excluding TOPs of 13.1%.
    explanation: >-
      Both figures, because either alone misleads: a third including terminations of pregnancy and
      an eighth without them. Eighty-four fetuses.
  - reference: PMID:39482803
    reference_title: >-
      Growth velocity of fetal sacrococcygeal teratoma as predictor of perinatal morbidity and
      mortality: multicenter study.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      The overall survival rate after prenatal diagnosis of isolated SCT was 75% (n = 41 of 55).
    explanation: >-
      A second series' figure for non-syndromic tumours, 55 fetuses across five centres.
  - reference: PMID:29734172
    reference_title: >-
      Preemptive Delivery and Immediate Resection for Fetuses with High-Risk Sacrococcygeal
      Teratomas.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      One death was due to pulmonary hypoplasia in a neonate with significant intra-abdominal tumor
      burden, and the other was due to in utero tumor rupture.
    explanation: >-
      The two deaths among eleven fetuses delivered early: one from pulmonary hypoplasia with a
      large intra-abdominal tumour, and one from tumour rupture in the womb.
  - reference: PMID:23432104
    reference_title: >-
      High prevalence of sacrococcygeal teratoma in Finland - a nationwide population-based study.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Tumours were detected in utero in 55% of the pregnancies with SCT.
    explanation: >-
      The Finnish national register's share found before birth.
  - reference: PMID:26454470
    reference_title: >-
      Sacrococcygeal teratoma: A population-based study of incidence and prenatal prognostic
      factors.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      A prenatal diagnosis was made in 74% of cases
    explanation: >-
      The share found before birth in a southern Swedish series; its abstract does not say which
      group it is counted over.
  - reference: PMID:18973151
    reference_title: >-
      Sacrococcygeal teratoma over two decades: birth prevalence, prenatal diagnosis and clinical
      outcomes.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      There was a prenatal diagnosis in 50% of cases.
    explanation: >-
      The share found before birth in a regional database; its abstract does not give the
      denominator.
  - reference: PMID:39482803
    reference_title: >-
      Growth velocity of fetal sacrococcygeal teratoma as predictor of perinatal morbidity and

    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Fifty-five fetuses were included, diagnosed with isolated SCT at a median gestational age of

    explanation: >-
      The median of 22 weeks, in a multicentre series of 55 fetuses.
  - reference: PMID:15192290
    reference_title: >-
      Sonographic prognostic factors in prenatal diagnosis of SCT.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-

    explanation: >-

  - reference: PMID:39753205
    reference_title: >-
      Proposal of a novel index in assessing perinatal mortality in prenatal diagnosis of

    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-

    explanation: >-

- phase: Neonatal resection
  notes: >-
    Most patients are operated on after birth. The operation decides what follows: completeness of
    resection and the histology of the specimen are the factors the recurrence literature keeps
    returning to, and a review cited on the resection row adds tumour spillage and failure to remove
    the coccyx.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:33906346
    reference_title: >-
      Sacrococcygeal Teratoma : A Tumor at the Center of Embryogenesis.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Most patients with SCT are operated on after birth.
    explanation: >-
      Where the default sits, from a review of this disease.
  - reference: PMID:33906346
    reference_title: >-
      Sacrococcygeal Teratoma : A Tumor at the Center of Embryogenesis.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Complete surgical resection is the key for tumor control, and the anatomical location of the
      tumor determines the surgical approaches.
    explanation: >-
      What the operation is for and what shapes it.
- phase: Recurrence
  duration: many recurrences within 1 to 6 years, some at 20 years
  notes: >-
    About one in ten children recur and about a third of those recurrences are malignant. The interval is the part that sets the follow-up: many recurrences fall within one to six years, in
    the pooled review's own word, and some are twenty years out. The risk of malignancy at initial resection rises with age and plateaus at six
    years, which is why delay matters.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:39248311
    reference_title: >-
      Malignant transformation and tumour recurrence in sacrococcygeal teratoma: a global,
      retrospective cohort study.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      The risk of malignant transformation of the initial tumour was 3.3, 5.1, 10.1, and 32.9% at
      age 3 months, 6 months, 1 year, and 2 years, respectively.
    explanation: >-
      The age gradient, in 3407 children from 145 institutes in 62 countries. A tenfold rise between
      three months and two years is the argument for operating early.
  - reference: PMID:33142194
    reference_title: >-
      Malignant recurrence after mature Sacrococcygeal teratoma: A meta-analysis and review of the
      literature.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Many recurrences occurred within 1-6 years, however some occurred as long as 20 years after
      initial diagnosis.
    explanation: >-
      The interval, pooled from 22 articles. The twenty-year tail is why the next sentence asks for
      at least six years of follow-up rather than two.
  - reference: PMID:33142194
    reference_title: >-
      Malignant recurrence after mature Sacrococcygeal teratoma: A meta-analysis and review of the
      literature.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Treatment of mature SCTs with resection alone requires thorough follow-up of at least 6 years.
    explanation: >-
      The recommendation that follows, and the one the alpha-fetoprotein surveillance row
      implements.
- phase: Long-term survivorship
  notes: >-
    Survival is high. What survivors carry is functional: in the Dutch national questionnaire study,
    at a median age of about ten, nearly half reported impaired bowel function or urinary
    incontinence and 40% an unacceptable scar, and these sequelae were correlated with reduced
    quality of life. The study's authors conclude that clinical variables cannot clearly identify
    the patients at higher risk; the one risk factor its abstract reports is tumour size above 500
    cm3, for the scar.

    Survival is also where this disease and the presacral teratoma of Currarino syndrome converge,
    at 94.9% against 96.9% in one global cohort, and malignancy is where they do not: malignant
    transformation at initial resection and malignant histology at recurrence are both several times
    higher here. Equal survival with unequal malignant risk is the reason the two are curated as
    separate entries rather than one.

    Later studies report predictors the Dutch national questionnaire study did not find, two of
    which, Altman type and histopathology, it tested and found not to be risk factors: in a 2023
    systematic review abnormal bladder function differed by Altman type, and adverse urological
    outcomes were commoner with immature or malignant tumours and in patients who needed
    reoperation; low gestational age independently predicted both urinary tract and bowel
    dysfunction in a Swedish series. Two later results agree with the Dutch null: the review found
    no significant association of bowel dysfunction with tumour characteristics, and a Scottish
    national cohort, in which constipation was the commonest bowel complaint, found no obvious
    predictive features at presentation for its bowel findings. A UK nationwide study found
    documented adverse bladder or bowel dysfunction in 36% of 165 patients. Most respondents in the
    Swedish series still reported good or very good quality of life.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:42250912
    reference_title: >-
      Malignant transformation of sacrococcygeal teratoma versus presacral teratoma in Currarino
      syndrome: Results of 'The SCT-study'.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Survival in both groups was equivalent at 94.9 % in SCT patients versus 96.9 % in CS patients
    explanation: >-
      The survival figure, from 3183 sacrococcygeal and 205 Currarino patients in a global cohort.
  - reference: PMID:42250912
    reference_title: >-
      Malignant transformation of sacrococcygeal teratoma versus presacral teratoma in Currarino
      syndrome: Results of 'The SCT-study'.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      The percentage of patients with malignant transformation at initial resection was higher in
      the SCT versus the CS group, 10.3 % and 31.9 % after one and two years, versus 4.2 % in CS
      patients after two years, respectively
    explanation: >-
      The difference behind the equal survival, and the reason this entry is kept separate from the
      Currarino one: the two concepts carry different malignant risk even where outcome converges.
  - reference: PMID:42250912
    reference_title: >-
      Malignant transformation of sacrococcygeal teratoma versus presacral teratoma in Currarino
      syndrome: Results of 'The SCT-study'.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Histology in recurrent teratoma was malignant in 35.4 % (n = 114) of SCT patients and 5.9 %
      (n = 1) of CS patients
    explanation: >-
      The same difference at recurrence, with both numerators. The single Currarino case behind the
      5.9% is why that figure carries no weight on its own.
  - reference: PMID:33906346
    reference_title: >-
      Sacrococcygeal Teratoma : A Tumor at the Center of Embryogenesis.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Survivors of SCT may suffer anorectal, urological, and sexual sequelae later in their life,
      and comprehensive evaluation and care are required.
    explanation: >-
      What survivorship involves, including an axis - sexual function - that the Dutch questionnaire
      study cited elsewhere in this entry did not measure.
  - reference: PMID:36127201
    reference_title: >-
      Long-term functional outcomes of sacrococcygeal teratoma - A systematic review of published
      studies exploring 'real world' outcomes.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: INDIRECT
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Higher Altman stage, unfavourable tumour biology and reoperation are associated with poor
      functional outcome(s).
    explanation: >-
      What goes with poor function in the systematic review. INDIRECT: a conclusion about poor
      function in general; the paragraph's figures are quoted separately.
  - reference: PMID:30420172
    reference_title: >-
      Functional outcome and health-related quality of life in patients with sacrococcygeal teratoma
      - a Swedish multicenter study.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Low gestational age was an independent predictor for both urinary tract and bowel dysfunction.
    explanation: >-
      Low gestational age as an independent predictor in the Swedish series.
  - reference: PMID:36229941
    reference_title: >-
      Sacrococcygeal teratoma: Long-term outcomes. A UK CCLG Surgeons Group Nationwide Study.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Fifty-nine (36%) of 165 patients had documented adverse bladder or bowel dysfunction.
    explanation: >-
      Bladder or bowel dysfunction in 36% of a UK nationwide cohort.
  - reference: PMID:30420172
    reference_title: >-
      Functional outcome and health-related quality of life in patients with sacrococcygeal teratoma
      - a Swedish multicenter study.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Good or very good QoL was reported by 56% of children aged 4-7 years, 90% of children aged
      8-17 years and 67% of the adults.
    explanation: >-
      Quality of life by age group in the Swedish series.
  - reference: PMID:36127201
    reference_title: >-
      Long-term functional outcomes of sacrococcygeal teratoma - A systematic review of published
      studies exploring 'real world' outcomes.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Abnormal bladder function was reported in 7/39 (18%) Altman Type I, 23/61 (37.7%) Type II,
      11/34 (32.4%) Type III, and 15/25 (60%) Type IV cases (p = 0.007).
    explanation: >-
      Abnormal bladder function by Altman type in the review.
  - reference: PMID:36127201
    reference_title: >-
      Long-term functional outcomes of sacrococcygeal teratoma - A systematic review of published
      studies exploring 'real world' outcomes.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Adverse urological outcomes were notably common in immature/malignant neoplasms vs benign

    explanation: >-
      Adverse urological outcomes with immature or malignant tumours and in patients who needed

  - reference: PMID:36127201
    reference_title: >-
      Long-term functional outcomes of sacrococcygeal teratoma - A systematic review of published
      studies exploring 'real world' outcomes.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Bowel dysfunction was evident in 19% index cases and constipation in 26% with no significant
      association(s) with tumour characteristics.
    explanation: >-
      No significant association of bowel dysfunction with tumour characteristics in the review.
  - reference: PMID:25005525
    reference_title: >-
      The long-term outcome of patients diagnosed with sacrococcygeal teratoma in childhood. A study
      of a national cohort.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL

    explanation: >-

  - reference: PMID:17560233

epidemiology:
- name: Sex distribution
  description: >-
    In a population-based birth defects registry in Hawaii, females accounted for 58.3% of the
    sacrococcygeal cases and 57.1% of the infant teratomas of all sites. The registry's teratoma
    rates, for all sites, differed by sex as by maternal race/ethnicity and geography, but apart
    from gestational age none of the differences was statistically significant, and its authors
    warn that the numbers are small. Two series give their own counts: among 55 neonates operated
    on between 1997 and 2016 who did not have a recurrence, excluding those who died and those with
    malignant germ cell tumours, 37 were female and 18 male; and an older series of 36 patients
    with benign neonatal tumours, treated from 1972 to 1990, reports 29 female patients as 89%, a
    share that does not fit 36 (29 of 36 is 81%). Three other sources restate a female excess of
    about 3:1, one of them 3:1 to 4:1, citing earlier work.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:16420341
    reference_title: >-
      Descriptive epidemiology of teratoma in infants, Hawaii, 1986-2001.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Females accounted for 57.1% of all cases and 58.3% of sacrococcygeal cases.
    explanation: >-
      The share of females, for the sacrococcygeal cases and for all sites; the abstract does not
      give the counts behind the two percentages.
  - reference: PMID:16420341

differential_diagnoses:
- name: Myelomeningocele
  description: >-
    A myelomeningocele and a sacrococcygeal teratoma can be taken for each other before birth. A
    case report describes a cystic tumour that mimicked a meningomyelocele; one centre, re-assessing
    two fetuses referred with a diagnosis of this tumour, found one to be healthy and the other to
    have a myelomeningocele; and a report of two presacral neuroblastomas names both conditions as
    the main clinical differentials in its two cases.
  disease_term:
    preferred_term: myelomeningocele
    term:
      id: MONDO:0019773
      label: myelomeningocele
  distinguishing_features:
  - >-
    In one case report, three-dimensional power Doppler imaging helped make the correct prenatal
    diagnosis of a cystic tumour that mimicked a meningomyelocele.
  - >-
    At one centre, assessment with both fetal MRI and ultrasound gave the right diagnosis in every
    fetus with this tumour assessed there, and re-assessment there re-classified one referral as a
    myelomeningocele.
  notes: >-
    This row's sources report correct diagnoses made with imaging, in one case report and at one
    centre, but give no feature that separates the two.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:19484739
    reference_title: >-
      Three-dimensional power Doppler sonography in the diagnosis of a cystic sacrococcygeal
      teratoma mimicking a meningomyelocele: A case report.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: INDIRECT
    quote_role: BACKGROUND
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      However, a cystic sacrococcygeal teratoma may be misdiagnosed as an anterior sacral
      meningomyelocele, especially when presenting as a posterior cystic mass.
    explanation: >-
      The misdiagnosis in the direction the case report describes, stated as its framing. Indirect:
      the report's term, anterior sacral meningomyelocele, sits between this row and the anterior
      sacral meningocele row; the case it reports mimicked a meningomyelocele.
  - reference: PMID:19484739
    reference_title: >-
      Three-dimensional power Doppler sonography in the diagnosis of a cystic sacrococcygeal
      teratoma mimicking a meningomyelocele: A case report.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      We report a case in which three-dimensional power Doppler imaging was helpful for making a
      correct prenatal diagnosis of a type 1 cystic sacrococcygeal teratoma, which mimicked a
      meningomyelocele.
    explanation: >-
      One case in which the tumour mimicked a meningomyelocele and three-dimensional power Doppler
      helped make the correct prenatal diagnosis.
  - reference: PMID:16985105
    reference_title: >-
      Diagnosis and characterization of fetal sacrococcygeal teratoma with prenatal MRI.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      The diagnosis of sacrococcygeal teratoma was accurate in all cases assessed at our center
      using both MRI and sonography.
    explanation: >-
      Fetal MRI and ultrasound together at one centre, which imaged 22 fetuses with the tumour by
      MRI.
  - reference: PMID:16985105
    reference_title: >-
      Diagnosis and characterization of fetal sacrococcygeal teratoma with prenatal MRI.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Two additional patients initially referred with the diagnosis of sacrococcygeal teratoma had a
      different diagnosis at reevaluation at our institution (healthy, n = 1; myelomeningocele, n =
      1).
    explanation: >-
      One referral for this tumour that turned out to be a myelomeningocele.
  - reference: PMID:33307929
    reference_title: >-
      Congenital Sacrococcygeal Neuroblastoma: A Report of Two Cases with Summary of Prior Published
      Cases.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: INDIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      The main clinical differential diagnoses were sacrococcygeal teratoma and meningomyelocele.
    explanation: >-
      Both conditions named as the differentials of two congenital presacral neuroblastomas.
      Indirect: the pairing with this tumour is drawn from a third condition's differential.
- name: Anterior sacral meningocele
  description: >-
    A meningocele in the presacral space, the space a sacrococcygeal teratoma with a presacral part
    occupies. A report of two siblings calls it and presacral teratoma related malformations that
    can both run in families, and both siblings had a presacral mass on imaging. Their family
    history of sacral bony abnormalities and anterior meningoceles resembles Currarino syndrome,
    although the abstract neither names the syndrome nor reports an anorectal malformation, and the
    siblings' presacral teratoma may be that syndrome's lesion rather than a sacrococcygeal
    teratoma; MONDO lists presacral teratoma as a synonym of sacrococcygeal teratoma, so the term
    alone does not settle it. A case report, cited here and in the myelomeningocele row, warns that
    a cystic sacrococcygeal teratoma may be misdiagnosed as an anterior sacral meningomyelocele. A
    fetal MRI series lists sacral meningocele, without saying anterior, among the differential
    diagnoses of the cystic forms of this tumour, and a review of caudal cell mass anomalies lists
    anterior sacral meningocele and sacrococcygeal teratoma among the forms that anomalous
    development of the caudal cell mass can take. No cited source reports an anterior sacral
    meningocele itself taken for a sacrococcygeal teratoma.
  disease_term:
    preferred_term: anterior sacral meningocele
    term:
      id: MONDO:0001147
      label: meningocele
  phenotypes:
  - name: Anterior sacral meningocele
    phenotype_term:
      preferred_term: anterior sacral meningocele
      term:
        id: HP:0007293
        label: Anterior sacral meningocele
  distinguishing_features:
  - >-
    No cited source gives an imaging feature that separates it from a presacral teratoma: the review
    of caudal cell mass anomalies says it describes the imaging criteria for diagnosing these
    anomalies, but its abstract states none. In the reported family the two lesions occurred in
    siblings with no bony sacral abnormality on imaging, and the authors advise CT or MRI looking
    for a presacral mass, rather than a plain radiograph looking for a sacral defect, to screen
    relatives.
  notes: >-
    MONDO has no term for anterior sacral meningocele: in the local MONDO build, label searches for
    "sacral meningocele" and "anterior sacral" returned nothing, and a search of labels and synonyms
    for "sacral meningocele" returned only Kousseff syndrome (MONDO:0016522), whose exact synonym is
    sacral meningocele-conotruncal heart defects syndrome. MONDO defines Currarino triad by
    anorectal malformations, a presacral mass (commonly anterior sacral meningocele or teratoma) and
    sacral anomalies. The row binds the broader meningocele as its disease term and the lesion
    itself as the HPO phenotype HP:0007293.

  - reference: PMID:11733920
    reference_title: >-
      Familial presacral masses: Screening pitfalls.

    directness: INDIRECT
    quote_role: BACKGROUND
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Anterior sacral meningocele (ASM) and presacral teratoma (PT) are related malformations. Both
      can have familial occurrence.
    explanation: >-
      The relation between the two lesions, as the report frames it. Indirect: presacral teratoma
      here is the familial lesion, not necessarily a sacrococcygeal teratoma.
  - reference: PMID:11733920
    reference_title: >-

    directness: INDIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL

  - reference: PMID:11733920
    reference_title: >-
      Familial presacral masses: Screening pitfalls.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: INDIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL

    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: INDIRECT
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      The lower spinal cord (conus medullaris), filum terminale and inferior lumbar and sacral nerve
      roots develop from the caudal cell mass, a remnant of the embryologic primitive streak
      composed of undifferentiated pluripotential cells. Anomalous caudal cell mass development can
      manifest as tight filum terminale, caudal dysgenesis, terminal myelocystocele, anterior sacral
      meningocele or sacrococcygeal teratoma.
    explanation: >-
      A review of caudal cell mass anomalies: the caudal cell mass is a remnant of the primitive
      streak composed of undifferentiated pluripotential cells, and anterior sacral meningocele and
      sacrococcygeal teratoma are among the forms its anomalous development can take. INDIRECT for
      the differential: a shared developmental origin in the review's account, not a report of
      one taken for the other.
- name: Presacral teratoma of Currarino syndrome
  description: >-
    A presacral teratoma in Currarino syndrome lies where a sacrococcygeal teratoma lies and looks
    like one, but behaves differently. In a Dutch national series of 205 patients with
    sacrococcygeal teratoma and 16 with Currarino syndrome, malignancy-free survival was lower in
    sacrococcygeal teratoma; in a global cohort of 3183 and 205 patients, malignancy was more often
    present in sacrococcygeal teratoma, with a risk of malignant transformation that rose with age,
    and was rare in Currarino syndrome.
  disease_term:
    preferred_term: Currarino syndrome
    term:
      id: MONDO:0008305
      label: Currarino triad
  distinguishing_features:
  - >-
    Malignancy-free survival in the Dutch series was 100% at two years in Currarino syndrome,
    against 80% at one year and 58% at two years in sacrococcygeal teratoma.
  - >-
    In the global cohort, malignancy was more often present in sacrococcygeal teratoma and its risk
    rose with age, and recurrence after resection was more often malignant; in Currarino patients
    malignancy was rare.
  notes: >-
    The syndrome's defining features, its gene and the other lesions that can form its presacral
    mass are curated in the Currarino_Triad entry and are not repeated here. This entry's
    progression section compares the two tumours' survival and malignant transformation from the
    global cohort, and its resection row cites the Dutch series.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:25746708
    reference_title: >-
      Malignant transformation in sacrococcygeal teratoma and in presacral teratoma associated with
      Currarino syndrome: a comparative study.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: BACKGROUND
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      The risk of malignant transformation of sacrococcygeal teratoma (SCT) and of presacral
      teratoma in Currarino syndrome (CS) may differ despite the similar position and appearance.
    explanation: >-
      Why the two are confused and why it matters, as the comparative study frames its question.
  - reference: PMID:25746708
    reference_title: >-
      Malignant transformation in sacrococcygeal teratoma and in presacral teratoma associated with
      Currarino syndrome: a comparative study.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Malignant transformation and teratoma recurrence were assessed in a national retrospective
      comparative analysis of 205 SCT and 16 CS patients treated in one of the six pediatric
      surgical centers in the Netherlands between January 1981 and December 2010.
    explanation: >-
      The Dutch series: national and retrospective, from the six paediatric surgical centres, 1981
      to 2010.
  - reference: PMID:25746708
    reference_title: >-
      Malignant transformation in sacrococcygeal teratoma and in presacral teratoma associated with

    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      The malignancy free survival of patients with SCT was lower than for patients with a presacral
      teratoma associated with CS (80% and 58% after one and two years in SCT versus 100% after two
      years in CS, p=0.017)
    explanation: >-
      The difference in malignancy-free survival, from 205 and 16 patients.
  - reference: PMID:25746708
    reference_title: >-

    supports: SUPPORT

    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Our data show that the risk of malignant transformation of a presacral teratoma in CS is
      small.
    explanation: >-
      The study's conclusion for the Currarino teratoma.
  - reference: PMID:42250912
    reference_title: >-
      Malignant transformation of sacrococcygeal teratoma versus presacral teratoma in Currarino
      syndrome: Results of 'The SCT-study'.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL

      The SCT-study shows that malignancy is more often present in SCT than in CS patients with an

    explanation: >-
      The global cohort's conclusion on malignancy, from 3183 sacrococcygeal and 205 Currarino

  - reference: PMID:42250912
    reference_title: >-

    supports: SUPPORT

    explanation: >-

- name: Presacral neuroblastoma
  description: >-
    Neuroblastoma can arise in the presacral part of the sympathetic chain and present at birth as a
    sacrococcygeal mass. In one newborn, imaging strongly suggested an Altman type III
    sacrococcygeal teratoma and histology showed neuroblastoma; a report of two congenital cases
    adds that such a tumour must be told apart from an immature or malignant neural lesion arising
    from a teratoma. A fetal MRI series lists low-lying neuroblastoma among the differential
    diagnoses of Altman type IV lesions.
  disease_term:
    preferred_term: presacral neuroblastoma
    term:
      id: MONDO:0005072
      label: neuroblastoma
  distinguishing_features:
  - >-
    Histology tells them apart: in two congenital cases the tumours lacked teratomatous tissue.
  - >-
    The two congenital cases also lacked germ cell serum markers, which the abstract does not name.
  notes: >-
    MONDO has no presacral, pelvic or sacral neuroblastoma term: in the local MONDO build, searches
    of labels and synonyms for "presacral neuroblastoma", "pelvic neuroblastoma" and "sacral
    neuroblastoma" returned nothing. The row binds neuroblastoma (MONDO:0005072), the disease term
    of this knowledge base's Neuroblastoma entry, so that it points at that entry; the narrower
    extracranial neuroblastoma (MONDO:0002749) would also be accurate.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:33307929
    reference_title: >-
      Congenital Sacrococcygeal Neuroblastoma: A Report of Two Cases with Summary of Prior Published
      Cases.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: BACKGROUND
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Neuroblastoma can arise from extra-adrenal sites in the paraspinal sympathetic chain,
      including the presacral region, where they must be differentiated from an immature or
      malignant neural lesion arising from a teratoma.
    explanation: >-
      Where the confusion lies, as the report's background states it.
  - reference: PMID:33307929
    reference_title: >-
      Congenital Sacrococcygeal Neuroblastoma: A Report of Two Cases with Summary of Prior Published
      Cases.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-

    explanation: >-
      What the two congenital cases lacked on pathology, teratomatous tissue and germ cell serum

  - reference: PMID:33307929
    reference_title: >-

    supports: SUPPORT

    explanation: >-

      Differential diagnoses include sacral chordoma, sacral meningocele, terminal myelocystocoele,

- name: Fetus in fetu
  description: >-
    A malformed fetus-like mass within its host. A systematic review of 241 single and 33 multiple
    cases weighs a teratoma theory against an identical twin theory, finds evidence for both, and
    calls a monozygotic twin of the host the most likely explanation. It can be misdiagnosed as a
    teratoma because the two look alike on ultrasound, and it is rare at the sacrococcygeal site,
    where teratoma is common. In the review, the mass was found before birth in 43 of the single
    cases, and in three quarters of those it was not suspected on imaging; sacrococcygeal teratoma
    is among the presumptive diagnoses the review lists for a mass in the abdominal cavity. In its
    discussion the review calls telling fetus in fetu apart from highly differentiated teratomas
    crucial: it calls a teratoma a neoplasm originating from embryonic pluripotent cells, with the
    potential to behave in a malignant fashion, and fetus in fetu a parasitic twin within its host.
  distinguishing_features:
  - >-
    A vertebral column or limb bones in the mass, with no immature elements: the systematic review
    calls a visible vertebral column or limb bones diagnostic and requires both conditions in its
    case definition, while noting that the defining criteria remain unclear. One or more long bones
    were detected in 131 of its 241 single cases, which the review says facilitated the diagnosis
    before surgery. A review of fetiform teratoma names cytogenetic studies as the gold standard for
    telling fetiform teratoma and fetus in fetu apart.
  - >-
    The site: 10 of the review's 241 single cases (4.1%) were sacrococcygeal, gluteal or perineal,
    against 174 (72.2%) retroperitoneal.
  - >-
    Fetiform teratoma, a germ cell tumour that can mimic a malformed fetus and also occurs at the
    sacrococcygeal site, lies on the teratoma side of the boundary; a review of it proposes the
    absence of a vertebral column and long bones as its criterion.
  - >-
    Organogenesis and a heartbeat: a case report's discussion calls well-differentiated
    organogenesis the key feature for telling fetus in fetu from teratoma, together with detection
    of a fetal heartbeat, citing earlier work. The systematic review, by contrast, documented heart
    or cardiac tissue in only 9 of its 241 single cases (3.7%) and calls heart tissue exceptionally
    rare in fetus in fetu.
  notes: >-
    No disease term is bound. MONDO has none: in the local MONDO build, searches of labels and
    synonyms for "fetus in fetu" and "fetus-in-fetu" returned nothing, and an OLS search of MONDO
    for "fetus in fetu" returned only unrelated terms, the first being Campylobacter fetus
    infectious disease (MONDO:0040728). NCIT has Fetus in Fetu (NCIT:C189052), but this slot takes
    MONDO terms only.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:39479419
    reference_title: >-
      Demystifying Fetus-in-fetu: A Systematic Review of Its Clinical and Pathological Attributes.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      A total of 249 case reports/case series comprising 241 single FIF cases and 33 multiple FIF
      cases were included for analysis.
    explanation: >-
      The size of the review, 241 single and 33 multiple cases; the site and long-bone percentages
      cited in this row are of the 241 single cases.
  - reference: PMID:39479419
    reference_title: >-
      Demystifying Fetus-in-fetu: A Systematic Review of Its Clinical and Pathological Attributes.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Other less common locations included intrathoracic (n = 11; 4.7%), head-and-neck region
      including oral cavity (n = 10; 4.1%), sacrococcygeal/gluteal/perineal (n = 10; 4.1%),
      intracranial (n = 9; 3.7%), and within the gonads (n = 9; 3.7%).
    explanation: >-
      How rarely it occurs at or near the sacrococcygeal site, pooled over 241 single cases.
  - reference: PMID:39479419
    reference_title: >-
      Demystifying Fetus-in-fetu: A Systematic Review of Its Clinical and Pathological Attributes.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      The retroperitoneum (n = 174; 72.2%) was the most common location, followed by intraperitoneal
      sites (n = 14; 5.8%).
    explanation: >-
      Its usual site, from the same pooled cases.
  - reference: PMID:39479419
    reference_title: >-
      Demystifying Fetus-in-fetu: A Systematic Review of Its Clinical and Pathological Attributes.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Demonstration of discernible vertebral column and/or tubular limb bones within a solid-cystic
      mass clinches the diagnosis of FIF.
    explanation: >-
      The feature that settles the diagnosis, as the review states it.
  - reference: PMID:39479419
    reference_title: >-
      Demystifying Fetus-in-fetu: A Systematic Review of Its Clinical and Pathological Attributes.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Hence, the defining criteria for the diagnosis of FIF remains unclear.
    explanation: >-
      The review's own caveat on where the boundary lies.
  - reference: PMID:39479419
    reference_title: >-

    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL

    explanation: >-

  - reference: PMID:39479419
    reference_title: >-
      Demystifying Fetus-in-fetu: A Systematic Review of Its Clinical and Pathological Attributes.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL

    explanation: >-

  - reference: PMID:39479419
    reference_title: >-
      Demystifying Fetus-in-fetu: A Systematic Review of Its Clinical and Pathological Attributes.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      The "teratoma theory" posits that FIF represents a specialized type of highly
      well-differentiated teratoma whereas the "identical twin theory" proposes that FIF arises from
      abnormalities in the twinning process.
    explanation: >-
      The two theories of origin the review weighs, by name.
  - reference: PMID:39479419
    reference_title: >-
      Demystifying Fetus-in-fetu: A Systematic Review of Its Clinical and Pathological Attributes.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL

    explanation: >-

  - reference: PMID:39479419
    reference_title: >-
      Demystifying Fetus-in-fetu: A Systematic Review of Its Clinical and Pathological Attributes.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-

    explanation: >-

  - reference: PMID:39479419
    reference_title: >-

  - reference: PMID:39479419
    reference_title: >-
      Demystifying Fetus-in-fetu: A Systematic Review of Its Clinical and Pathological Attributes.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL

    explanation: >-

  - reference: PMID:39479419
    reference_title: >-
      Demystifying Fetus-in-fetu: A Systematic Review of Its Clinical and Pathological Attributes.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Among the antenatally detected cases of singleton FIF, only in 25% of cases, a preoperative
      diagnosis of FIF was considered by the radiologist, or the physician performing scan. In
      remaining cases (75%), FIF was not suspected on imaging and the presumptive diagnoses
      considered included hepatic cyst, retroperitoneal teratoma, meconium peritonitis or ileus,
      encysted fetal ascites, mesenteric or omental cyst, adrenal tumor, neuroblastoma,
      sacrococcygeal teratoma, hemangioma if the tumor was found in the abdominal cavity
    explanation: >-

      in the abdominal cavity.
  - reference: PMID:40515865
    reference_title: >-
      Fetiform teratoma: a systematic review with insights into concepts and controversies in
      differentiating it from fetus-in-fetu.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Fetiform teratomas result from neoplastic processes of germ cells, while fetus-in-fetu arises

    explanation: >-

  - reference: PMID:40515865

  - reference: PMID:40515865
    reference_title: >-

  - reference: PMID:40515865
    reference_title: >-
      Fetiform teratoma: a systematic review with insights into concepts and controversies in

    supports: SUPPORT

    explanation: >-

  - reference: PMID:40041259
    reference_title: >-
      Fetus-in-fetu: mimicking teratoma on antenatal ultrasound.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: BACKGROUND
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      In contrast, a teratoma is most commonly found in the sacrococcygeal, gonadal, mediastinal,
      and CNS.
    explanation: >-
      The site contrast, in a case report's discussion.
  - reference: PMID:39479419
    reference_title: >-
      Demystifying Fetus-in-fetu: A Systematic Review of Its Clinical and Pathological Attributes.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      It is crucial to differentiate them from highly differentiated teratomas. Teratomas, despite
      containing well-organized structures, are neoplasms originating from embryonic pluripotent
      cells, exhibiting the potential to behave in a malignant fashion. On the contrary, FIF, as the
      name suggests, refers to a parasitic twin within its host.
    explanation: >-
      The review's own line between the two, in its discussion: telling fetus in fetu apart from
      highly differentiated teratomas is crucial, a teratoma being a neoplasm from embryonic
      pluripotent cells with the potential to behave in a malignant fashion, and fetus in fetu a
      parasitic twin.
  - reference: PMID:40041259
    reference_title: >-
      Fetus-in-fetu: mimicking teratoma on antenatal ultrasound.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT

    explanation: >-

    reference_title: >-

- name: Chordoma
  description: >-

discussions:
- discussion_id: sct_hydrops_predicts_or_not
  kind: CONTROVERSY
  status: OPEN
  prompt: >-
    Does fetal hydrops predict survival in sacrococcygeal teratoma?
  attaches_to:
  - phenotypes#Hydrops fetalis
  - pathophysiology#High-Output Cardiac State from Tumour Vascular Steal
  rationale: >-
    Two cited sources answer this in opposite directions and neither is obviously wrong. One reports
    hydrops as a potential risk factor for poor outcome at an odds ratio of 21, from 68 analysed fetuses
    of an 84-fetus cohort with eleven poor outcomes, and a meta-analysis lists it among the factors predictive of poor outcome. The other, a
    review of 157 fetuses split across open surgery, percutaneous intervention and no intervention,
    reports that hydrops and cardiac failure had no significant impact on survival. The disagreement
    may be about what is being predicted - outcome in the first, survival in the second - or about
    selection: the fetuses who develop hydrops are the ones offered intervention. No cited source
    reconciles them, and the entry carries both rather than choosing.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:37964422
    reference_title: >-
      Prognostic accuracy of factors associated with poor outcome in prenatally diagnosed
      sacrococcygeal teratoma: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Factors associated with poor outcome in fetuses with prenatally diagnosed SCT were
      cardiomegaly, hypervascular tumor, solid tumor morphology, fetal hydrops, and placentomegaly.
    explanation: >-
      One side, from a meta-analysis of eleven studies and 447 patients.
  - reference: PMID:38731178
    reference_title: >-
      Perinatal Outcomes of Intrauterine Interventions for Fetal Sacrococcygeal Teratoma Based on
      Different Surgical Techniques-A Systematic Review.
    supports: REFUTE
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      In our evaluation, we determined that the presence of fetal hydrops and cardiac failure had no
      significant impact on survival in SCT cases.
    explanation: >-
      The other side. REFUTE against the claim above, and recorded here rather than averaged into
      it.
  - reference: PMID:23845611
    reference_title: >-
      Tumor metrics and morphology predict poor prognosis in prenatally diagnosed sacrococcygeal
      teratoma: a 25-year experience at a single institution.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: BACKGROUND
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Some fetuses with sacrococcygeal teratoma (SCT) develop hydrops, but there is no consensus on
      an appropriate prognostic marker for poor prognosis.
    explanation: >-
      The absence of consensus, stated in those terms by a third study. It predates both sources
      above and the disagreement outlived it.
- discussion_id: sct_no_disease_model
  kind: HUMAN_MODEL_MISMATCH
  status: OPEN
  prompt: >-
    Every cited animal model of teratoma is gonadal. Does the mouse germ cell teratoma mechanism
    apply to a tumour whose defining feature is that the germ cell never reached a gonad?
  attaches_to:
  - pathophysiology#Epigenetic Reprogramming to a Pluripotent State
  - animal_models#Mouse
  rationale: >-
    The reprogramming step in this entry's chain is supported entirely by mouse work, and every
    mouse in the cited literature has a testicular or ovarian teratoma. No sacrococcygeal model
    exists in any species in this corpus; the only non-rodent animal report is an oropharyngeal
    teratoma in a goat. That matters more here than in most entries, because the thing being
    modelled is a cell that failed to reach the gonad, and the model contains one. The mouse work
    also fails in a way that is informative: mutating Dnd1 alone gives germ cell loss rather than
    teratoma, and the strains built to make testicular teratomas made ovarian ones instead.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:33568756
    reference_title: >-
      MC4R mutant mice develop ovarian teratomas.
    supports: NO_EVIDENCE
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: BACKGROUND
    evidence_source: MODEL_ORGANISM
    snippet: >-
      This suggests that other genes are involved in teratoma formation.
    explanation: >-
      The authors' own reading of the first failure. NO_EVIDENCE: it records that the mechanism is
      incomplete rather than bearing on whether it transfers to this disease.
  - reference: PMID:29378702
    reference_title: >-
      Dnd1-mediated epigenetic control of teratoma formation in mouse.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: INDIRECT
    quote_role: BACKGROUND
    evidence_source: MODEL_ORGANISM
    snippet: >-
      Spontaneous testicular teratoma develops from primordial germ cells (PGCs) in embryos;
      however, the molecular mechanisms underlying teratoma formation are not fully understood.
    explanation: >-
      The state of the mechanism, and the organ it was worked out in. BACKGROUND: it is the paper's
      framing of the problem.
- discussion_id: sct_prenatal_threshold_unsettled
  kind: KNOWLEDGE_GAP
  status: OPEN
  prompt: >-
    Which prenatal measurement, at which threshold, should decide whether a fetus with
    sacrococcygeal teratoma is offered intervention?
  attaches_to:
  - diagnosis#Prenatal ultrasound with tumour volume to fetal weight ratio
  rationale: >-
    At least ten thresholds compete in the cited literature and none has displaced the others:
    tumour volume to fetal weight ratio at 0.12 before 24 weeks and 0.11 before 32 weeks; the same
    ratio at 0.095 for fetal outcome against 0.12 for maternal operative risk; total tumour volume
    over estimated fetal weight at 0.16; a solid tumour volume index at 0.09; a morphology score of
    3; tumour volume over head circumference plus polyhydramnios at 3.0; growth velocity at 7 mm per
    week; a solid tumour to head volume ratio of 1; tumour volume over biparietal diameter at 60 cm3
    per cm; and a volume growth rate above 18.01 cm3 per week and a volume above 245 cm3. The
    ratio's validation study reports that none of the factors associated with poor prognosis was an
    independent predictor on multivariate analysis; the growth velocity study reports that its
    measure was the only one that survived stepwise regression, and a second growth series that only
    the volume growth rate survived adjustment. One series finds the solid tumour volume index a
    better predictor than total volume over fetal weight, and another finds no significant
    difference between the ratio and the head-circumference composite. Each comes from 10 to 79
    fetuses. The entry records all of them, with their denominators, because a reader choosing
    between them needs to see that the choice has not been made.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:23845611
    reference_title: >-
      Tumor metrics and morphology predict poor prognosis in prenatally diagnosed sacrococcygeal
      teratoma: a 25-year experience at a single institution.
    supports: NO_EVIDENCE
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: BACKGROUND
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Some fetuses with sacrococcygeal teratoma (SCT) develop hydrops, but there is no consensus on
      an appropriate prognostic marker for poor prognosis.
    explanation: >-
      The gap stated as a gap. NO_EVIDENCE: it records the absence rather than bearing on which
      marker is right.
  - reference: PMID:25783370
    reference_title: >-
      Predictors of poor prognosis in prenatally diagnosed sacrococcygeal teratoma: A
      multiinstitutional review.
    supports: SUPPORT
    directness: DIRECT
    quote_role: BACKGROUND
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Attempts at defining predictors of poor outcome in fetal sacrococcygeal teratoma (SCT) have
      been hampered by small patient numbers.
    explanation: >-
      Why the gap persists, from a three-centre series that evaluated 79 fetuses and excluded eleven
      terminations.
- discussion_id: sct_altman_unsourceable
  kind: KNOWLEDGE_GAP
  status: OPEN
  prompt: >-
    The Altman types are the postnatal classification most frequently referenced for this tumour.

    Types II and III carry an odds ratio of 1.6 for recurrence in the largest cohort, and the
    classification predicts no long-term sequela in the Dutch national questionnaire study, although
    a 2023 systematic review found that abnormal bladder function differed by Altman type, lowest in
    type I (18%) and highest in type IV (60%). The entry records those results and does not curate
    the types. The primary source, the 1974 American Academy of Pediatrics Surgical Section survey,
    caches with an empty body under both its PMID and its DOI - both files are committed with this

    from a covariate column. Two imaging sources cited here for other findings restate all four
    types, citing earlier work, and one gives the usual share of each; they are quoted below and
    would let the types be curated with evidence behind them. The two restatements differ in detail:

    and they word type IV differently. HPO's own text definition of HP:0030736, the term this entry
    binds for the mass, also states all four types, and HPO carries separate terms for types I, II
    and III with their own definitions and one for the presacral type IV, but an ontology definition
    is not a literature source and cannot be an evidence snippet.

notes: >-
  Most cited sources are case reports, case series, cohorts and registry studies, or reviews and
  meta-analyses of those. A few are of other kinds, such as mouse work, laboratory
  reference-interval work on healthy infants, genetic association studies and a single-arm treatment
  study. No randomised trial of this disease is cited. Most cached sources are abstracts, so a
  statement here about what the literature does not contain is mostly a statement about abstracts.
  Denominators are named wherever the source gives one, because they differ by nearly three orders
  of magnitude - a global cohort of 3407 children, a national register of 124 cases, prenatal series
  of tens of fetuses, and a first report of radiofrequency ablation in four. Some figures come
  without a count, because their source does not say what they are counted over, such as the
  regional database's prenatal detection rate and the Hawaiian registry's percentages of females.

  Numbers that disagree are kept, each with its source. The four population-based figures in the
  prevalence section run from 3.7 to 9.3 per 100,000. The highest, Finland's total prevalence of 1
  in 10,700, counts stillbirths and terminations over pregnancies, where the other three are rates
  per live birth; it is two to four times the range previously reported, 1 in 27,000 to 1 in 40,000,
  and twice the Hawaii figure of 0.43 per 10,000 live births, and the Finnish authors say this may
  be a true population difference or may be more complete ascertainment. And fetal hydrops is
  reported as a strong predictor of poor outcome by two sources and as having no significant impact
  on survival by a third, which is recorded as a controversy rather than averaged.

  The mechanism is modelled on mouse gonadal teratoma. The reprogramming step has a named chromatin
  mechanism in mouse testis and no counterpart in any human sacrococcygeal tumour in this corpus, and
  no animal model of a sacrococcygeal teratoma is cited at all. That is recorded on the model links
  and again as a discussion, because the thing being modelled is a germ cell that never reached a
  gonad and every model contains one.
review_notes: >-
  Written from cached sources only, by hand. Where a claim rests on a handful of patients, the
  explanation says so rather than leaving it to the reader to look up the denominator.

  Several things are deliberately absent. The Altman classification is not defined in this entry:
  its primary source is cached with an empty body under both its identifiers, and the question is
  recorded as a discussion rather than filled in from memory.
  No gene in the genetic section is claimed for this tumour
  specifically: all four susceptibility loci come from studies that pool germ cell tumours across
  sites, and the strongest reported effect for one of them is in testis. The two mouse models carry no bound gene, because a model organism's own gene takes its
  model-organism database identifier and none could be resolved from any source available here; the
  human identifier would have been wrong rather than approximate. One strain qualifier is kept because its
  source gives it: Dnd1 mutation enhances teratoma formation in 129/Sv. The second mouse paper says
  Dnd1-mutant mice show germ cell loss, and gives no strain for that sentence, so whether the two
  results disagree cannot be settled from what is cached here.
